paper.abstract: We derive a local fixed-point formula for the equivariant index of Heisenberg elliptic operators on closed contact manifolds equipped with an action of a compact Lie group preserving the contact form. The formula expresses the character of the equivariant index in terms of a cyclic-cohomological character of the noncommutative Heisenberg principal symbol. The main new ingredient is the construction of traces, one on each fixed-point set, defined by integration over twisted conjugacy classes in the Heisenberg group. The proof proceeds by a K-theoretic reduction to the equivariant index theorem of our paper "Toeplitz operators on contact manifolds and equivariant K-homology".
paper.title: An equivariant index theorem for the Heisenberg calculus

paper.abstract: We propose a definition of symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories as special left double $(\infty,n)$-fibrations over the category of finite pointed sets. The definition makes sense in a general model of $(\infty,n)$-categories, under a mild condition on its discrete objects, and when the model is left proper and combinatorial we construct model structures whose fibrant objects are exactly these fibrations. For $n=1$ we show that the definition recovers Lurie's symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories: the homotopy theory of special left double $(\infty,1)$-fibrations is equivalent to that of special coCartesian fibrations over the category of finite pointed sets. The equivalence is realized by an explicit Quillen equivalence, and two constructions, the staircase and coCartesian strings, translate between the two descriptions.
paper.title: An internal approach to symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories

paper.abstract: We construct a topos for Borel mathematics: statements which are true in Borel mathemaics correspond in a precise way to statements which are true in the internal logic of this topos. We investigate several other properties of this topos, including proving that it satisfies a Borel analogue of the Church-Turing thesis: the statement that every function on a standard Borel space is Borel. We also show that an earlier construction of a similar "Borel topos" by van Osdol does not suit these purposes because of an error in that paper.
paper.title: The Borel Topos

paper.abstract: The positive-characteristic analogue of motivic cohomology with coefficients in an Anderson A-motive M over a function field of transcendence degree one was introduced in an earlier work of the author. In this paper, we prove that, when M arises as the dual of the A-motive of an Anderson module E that is abelian, uniformizable, and has everywhere good reduction, the corresponding A-motivic cohomology coincides with the module of Taelman units of E, up to a twist by the module of K\"ahler differentials of A. To this end, we recast the theory of Anderson generating functions in the spirit of earlier work of Maurischat and the author on special functions.
paper.title: A Barsotti-Weil isomorphism for Taelman units

paper.abstract: For a finite group $G$, we characterize the $2$-slices of $G$-spectra in the regular slice filtration in terms of their homotopy Mackey functors and $k$-invariant. We explicitly compute this for cyclic $p$-groups and the alternating group $A_4$.
paper.title: Characterizing $2$-slices over finite groups

paper.abstract:
We study stable equivalences defined by bimodule tensor identities over a commutative ring $R$. For the $R$-split exact structure, these identities preserve positive Hochschild homology and positive Hochschild cohomology with its cup product, Gerstenhaber bracket and, in prime characteristic, restricted power. A triangular comparison also identifies the relative singular Hochschild cochain complexes as $B_\infty$-algebras. For reduced pairs of finite-dimensional Frobenius algebras over an algebraically closed field, with diagonalizable Nakayama automorphisms, we construct compatible Frobenius functionals and compare the Tate--Hochschild BV operators in all degrees.
  For flat algebras over $R$ we give a Hochschild-cohomological criterion for comparing marked associative deformations. It applies to biadjoint Morita-type pairs and, by reduction, to all stable equivalences of Morita type between finite-dimensional algebras over any field. We compare the Bezrukavnikov--Ginzburg maps in characteristic zero by using a common triangular deformation or by lifting a two-sided tilting complex. We also compare marked module deformations over local Artin rings and their augmented universal rings.
  Further applications concern connected outer automorphism group schemes over perfect fields, the kernels of the quotient maps on ordinary algebraic $K$-theory, and the nonconnective $K$-theory of enhanced relative singularity categories. We construct biadjoint representatives over Henselian Noetherian local rings and relative stable tensor functors for almost $\nu$-stable derived equivalences. We also answer a question of Abe and Hoshino about preservation of the Gorenstein condition in a fixed codimension.
paper.title: Hochschild operations and other invariants of stable equivalences of Morita type

paper.abstract:
In a recent paper, Tobias Fritz and the second author identified $\sigma C^*$-algebras as a tentative noncommutative analogue of measurable spaces. We advance this analogy by establishing monadicity of $\sigma C^*$-algebras over $C^*$-algebras and proving several results of interest to both the category theory and operator algebra communities. In detail, we show that:
  - The associated probabilistic morphisms, $\sigma$-cpu maps, admit a description via a comonad closely related to the Giry monad. Equivalently, $\sigma$-cpu maps can be characterized by a universal property.
  - The category of $\sigma C^*$-algebras and $\sigma$-homomorphisms is locally $\aleph_1$-presentable.
  - $\sigma C^*$-algebras have a tensor product induced by the maximal tensor product of $C^*$-algebras and satisfying an analogous universal property.
  - The notion of CP-instruments, defined as $\sigma$-additive assignments from a $\sigma$-algebra to a space of completely positive maps, can be adapted to this setting by taking as target the set of $\sigma$-normal completely positive maps between $\sigma C^*$-algebras. This yields a bijective correspondence with $\sigma$-cpu maps out of the tensor product of the previous item.
paper.title: Monadicity of noncommutative measurable spaces over $C^{\ast}$-algebras

paper.abstract: Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian $n$-manifold, $n\geq 2$, and suppose that either $M$ is negatively curved, or that it is a locally symmetric space of non-compact type. Via integration over straight simplices, every top-degree bounded differential form $\omega\in \Omega_b^n(M)$ defines a bounded cohomology class in $H^n_b(M)$. We prove that every such class belongs to the annihilator of the cup product in the whole graded algebra $H^{\geq 1}_b(M)$. In the case of closed orientable surfaces, this generalizes a result of Marasco, and, via transfer, provides a new proof of the fact that the cup product of the bounded Euler class of $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ with itself vanishes. Our result also applies to degree-3 bounded classes constructed by Soma and Farre, thus showing that, for surface groups and for free groups, the annihilator of the cup product is infinite dimensional also in degree 3.
paper.title: Cup products with volume classes in bounded cohomology

paper.abstract: We construct a Poisson bracket on the cohomology of locally constant prefactorization algebras on $\mathbb{R}^m$ that provides an obstruction to formality in every dimension $m\geqslant 2$. Our construction combines colored obstruction sequences to formality with linking spheres and generalizes the two-dimensional bracket of Bruinsma, Schenkel, and Vicedo. We use it to extend their non-formality theorem for Lie algebra factorization envelopes to all higher dimensions. We also establish new non-formality results for factorization envelopes of Lie algebras, their compactifications and generalizations to $L_\infty$-algebras, free BF-type theories, higher abelian Chern-Simons theories and their compactifications.
paper.title: Non-formality of prefactorization algebras

paper.abstract:
Homotopy theory has traditionally been approached either through topological spaces or through categories of presheaves on suitable combinatorial categories, a perspective subsumed by Grothendieck's theory of test categories. In this paper, we develop a more algebraic viewpoint: homotopy types can be represented by actions of a single monoid on sets.
  This monoid is obtained by identifying all the objects of the semisimplicial category while retaining its face operators. Every CW homotopy type is the classifying space of the translation category of one of its actions, and its truncation at dimension n is finitely presented and realizes exactly the homotopy types of dimension at most n.
  The construction rests on a general result: every set-valued functor on a small category freely generates an action of its universal monoid, and its category of elements is a full coreflective subcategory of the resulting translation category. Hence every weak test category gives rise to a monoid whose actions realize all homotopy types; when the category has more than one object, however, this monoid is not itself a weak test category, so that a single monoid may realize all homotopy types without modelling homotopy theory as a localization. The obstruction lies in identifying objects, not in having a single one: there are strict test categories with a single object, such as the monoid of all self-maps of an infinite set and a countable monoid of primitive recursive functions.
paper.title: One monoid to realize them all: a master monoid for homotopy types

paper.abstract: We describe a product between framed 1-flow categories and show that it satisfies the expected Cartan formula on its second Steenrod squares. We also describe a dual framed 1-flow category and show that, like the Spanier-Whitehead dual of spectra, the homology groups of a framed 1-flow category can be shown to be isomorphic to the cohomology groups of its dual and that this isomorphism can be shown to cooperate with the framed 1-flow category structure in a suitable sense.
paper.title: Products and duality for framed 1-flow categories

paper.abstract: We construct infinitely many closed oriented smooth 4-manifolds which are all stably diffeomorphic but pairwise not homotopy equivalent. Our examples are distinguished by their second homotopy modules, and provide the first examples which demonstrate that stable diffeomorphism does not determine the second homotopy module. They have fundamental group $(\mathbb{Z}/4)^4*\mathbb{Z}$ and arise as doubles of presentation 2-complexes. In contrast, we give criteria for isomorphism of second homotopy modules of doubles of 2-complexes, covering finite abelian, quaternion, dihedral and symmetric fundamental groups. We also establish non-injectivity of the doubling construction by showing that there exist homotopically distinct presentation 2-complexes over $Q_{28}$ whose doubles are homotopy equivalent.
paper.title: Second homotopy modules and infinite homotopy stable classes of four-manifolds

paper.abstract: We study topological inference for the degree-Cech bifiltration from noisy samples of a manifold. Under a model combining uniform sampling on the manifold with uniform noise, we show that suitable choices of the radius and degree parameters recover the homotopy type of the underlying manifold with high probability. The analysis explains how the degree parameter suppresses sufficiently distant outliers while the radius scale captures topological signals. Our results provide theoretical support for the common intuition that degree bifiltrations carry meaningful topological information in the presence of noise.
paper.title: Topological Inference for degree-Cech complexes

paper.abstract: The vanishing of the L^2-Betti numbers of the universal covering of a closed manifold is an obstruction to fibring over the circle. When the L^2-Betti numbers vanish we introduce a secondary obstruction based on the asymptotic behaviour of the twisted L^2-torsion function at 0 and infinity. We provide a number of examples showing the invariant is indeed non-trivial.
paper.title: Twisted $L^2$-torsion functions obstruct fibring over the circle

paper.abstract: On 20 November 2026, Levent Alpöge released a commentless Lean 4 formalization, developed with Claude, proving the Riemann hypothesis and the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for all Dirichlet $L$-functions across $175{,}187$ source modules ($17{,}374{,}215$ lines; $1{,}484{,}733$ compiled kernel declarations). While independent kernel replays confirm formal validity from the three standard Lean axioms, no conventional mathematical paper accompanied the archive. We give a compact, self-contained five-stage mathematical blueprint of the argument from a windowed prime-power inequality to the five root theorems of Main.lean, anchored to an index of $240$ kernel-live declarations ($233$ public declarations across $104$ modules plus $7$ structure fields and Mathlib theorems), each pinned by exact source line, kernel export_id, and five-root reachability bitmask in solution.ndjson. First, a gamma-localized Landau derivative dichotomy excludes zeros in $\operatorname{Re} s > \theta$ from a one-sided bound $G_{\mathcal{F}}(y) \le C y^\theta$ on arbitrarily distant windows $[Z, Z^{3/2}]$ without global sign assumptions. Second, character orthogonality on $G = (\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^2 \times H$ over CM towers of degree $[E:\mathbb{Q}] = 4n \asymp x^{2+8\varepsilon}$ isolates odd inert prime powers via $\mathrm{ASK} - \mathrm{MAIN} = \mathrm{De}$. Third, along an $m$-step unitary theta ladder ($m \asymp x^{1/2-\varepsilon/16}$, $k \asymp x^{9/2+10\varepsilon}$), supersingular height-$2$ Lubin-Tate formal groups supply net $\ell$-adic jet valuation rate $\gamma_\ell = \frac{1}{\ell - 1} - \frac{1}{\ell^2 - 1} = \frac{\ell}{\ell^2 - 1} = \sum_{e\,\mathrm{odd}} \ell^{-e}$ against rate $0$ at split primes. Fourth, averaging a four-clause Bost-Arakelov slope chain with Chowla-Selberg CM period evaluation cancels intermediate heights, while block-shared divisor budgets replace $O(m^2)$ prefix compounding ($x^{2/3}$ barrier) by $O(m)$; a four-wall linear program over $(a, \kappa)$ at $\nu = 2$ uniquely selects $(a, \kappa) = (1/2, 9/2)$ and $\theta_* = 1/2$. We also record three classical consequences, resolve archive homonym collisions, and verify $27$ companion algebraic, LP, Lubin-Tate, slope-telescope, and carrier-isomorphism theorems in a zero-import Lean 4.33.1 module.
paper.title: Mathematical Blueprint and 240-Declaration Kernel Index for the Alpöge–Claude Lean 4 Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis

paper.abstract: For a non-empty connected small category we compare four properties: being filtered; exactness of colimits of abelian groups; Grothendieck's total asphericity, which says that colimits of simplicial sets over the category are homotopy colimits; and being quasi-filtered, which means that two arrows with a common source can be completed to a commutative square and that two parallel arrows are equalized by an integral combination of arrows whose coefficients sum to 1. Each implies the next. We give a category of finite ordered hypergraphs that is totally aspherical and whose colimits are exact over no non-zero ring, and we show that the category of finite ordered two-graphs (sets of triples that meet every four-element set in an even number of triples) is quasi-filtered and not totally aspherical. With the example of Isbell and Mitchell, the three implications are strict. A conjecture in Grothendieck's Les Dérivateurs, that totally aspherical categories are filtered, is therefore false; it holds for sifted categories, those over which colimits of sets commute with finite products.
paper.title: Exact, total and filtered small categories

paper.abstract: An element of the profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller group $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ of Drinfeld is a pair $(\lambda,f)$, with $\lambda$ a unit of $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ and $f$ in the free profinite group $\widehat F_2$ on $x$ and $y$, that satisfies three relations and for which $x\mapsto x^\lambda$, $y\mapsto f^{-1}y^\lambda f$ is an automorphism of $\widehat F_2$. Lochak and Schneps asked in 2006 whether this last requirement follows from the others, and whether it holds with no relation at all (Question 1.1 of their list of open problems). We prove that it follows, and from less: if $\lambda\in1+2\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ and $f\in\widehat F_2$ satisfy the two-cycle and three-cycle relations (I) and (II), then $\lambda$ is a unit and the endomorphism is an automorphism. The pentagon relation is not used. Relation (I) alone does not suffice: for $\lambda=1$ and $f=xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$ the endomorphism is not surjective. It follows that the Grothendieck-Teichmüller monoid, in the profinite form of Horel and of Boavida de Brito, Horel and Robertson, is equal to its group of units; that every endomorphism of the profinite operad of parenthesized braids that fixes the objects is an automorphism; and, by their theorems, that every homotopy endomorphism of the profinite completion of the little 2-discs operad, or of the genus zero surface operad, is a homotopy automorphism. The proof counts boundary components of finite covers in homology. An endomorphism of the profinite completion of the fundamental group of a compact surface with boundary that sends every boundary generator to a conjugate of a unit power of a boundary generator, bijectively on boundary components, is an automorphism; on a sphere with at least three holes the exponents of such an endomorphism are equal, and are zero or a unit. The criterion for unit exponents and the case of unit $\lambda$ were produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode) and checked by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high. Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max checked them again, found the statements for exponents that are not assumed to be units and the example above, and wrote this text. Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max checked these additions independently. No human has checked any of it.
paper.title: The profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller monoid is a group, on a question of Lochak and Schneps

paper.abstract:
We construct a solidification functor $\LH$ on condensed anima by localizing at the maps inverted by solid integral chains. A pointed connected nilpotent condensed anima is $\Hsol$-local precisely when its fundamental group admits a finite central series with solid abelian factors and its higher homotopy groups are solid. For simply connected condensed anima, we construct a natural strongly convergent spectral sequence \[ E^2_{p,q}=L_ps(\pi_qX)\Longrightarrow\pi_{p+q}\LH X \]
  where $L_ps$ denotes the $p$-th derived functor of the abelian solidification.
paper.title: Unstable Solidification

paper.abstract: For certain complex-oriented $K(n)$-local cohomology theories, we establish equivariant localization formulas for global Kuranishi charts and a Riemann-Roch formula. We apply these formulas to compute the genus-zero Gromov-Witten invariants of $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(-1)\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(-1)$ at odd primes, obtaining a residue formula in terms of the formal group law of the chosen complex orientation. As an application, we derive a multiple-cover formula expressing the genus-zero Morava $K$-theoretic Gromov-Witten invariants of closed symplectic Calabi-Yau threefolds in terms of their Gopakumar-Vafa invariants.
paper.title: Equivariant Localization for $K(n)$-Local Gromov-Witten Invariants with Applications to Gopakumar-Vafa Invariants

paper.abstract: The purpose of this note is to provide a modern treatment of Dwyer's tame homotopy theory and extend it to non-simply connected spaces, exploiting a connection with the work of Heuts on the Goodwillie tower of the identity. As an application, we construct spectral Lie algebraic models for Hess's $r$-mild homotopy theory.
paper.title: Tame homotopy theory and the Goodwillie tower of the identity

paper.abstract: We show that transverse intersections between smooth $\mathbb{C}_p$-analytic manifolds in $\mathbb{C}_p^n$ and perfectoid Banach--Colmez spaces of complementary $\mathbb{C}_p$-dimension are $n$-dimensional $\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic manifolds. In the case of the Banach--Colmez space $\mathrm{BC}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$, this is a strong form of the relativistic $p$-adic sunscreen conjecture. These results hold more generally with $\mathbb{C}_p$ replaced by an arbitrary complete algebraically closed extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and we also establish some non-linear analogs for infinite level Lubin--Tate spaces.
paper.title: $\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic intersections of $\mathbb{C}_p$-analytic manifolds with perfectoid Banach--Colmez spaces

paper.abstract: We construct a stack, which generalizes the notion of the arithmetic jet space functor constructed by Borger using the generalized Witt vector constructions. A priori we con- struct the jet space functor for prestacks, consequently showing that this functor preserves stacks. We then proceed to show the representability of the jet space functor applied to a representable morphism of stacks thereby showing that the jet space functor preserves algebraic and Deligne-Mumford Stacks. We also discuss the properties of morphisms preserved under the jet functor
paper.title: Arithmetic jet stacks

paper.abstract:
We construct a presentable, stable \(\infty\)-category \( KK\), and exhibit it as the target of the universal functor from the category of bornological algebras into cocomplete, stable \(\infty\)-categories, preserving filtered colimits, and satisfying smooth homotopy invariance, excision, and stabilisation with respect to Schatten-class or smooth compact operators. We also construct a bivariant \(K\)-theory \(
KK\) for suitably nuclear bornological algebras, and show that it is a right Bousfield localisation of \( KK\). The category \(
KK\) is symmetric monoidal and admits a bivariant Chern character to local cyclic homology. The categories \(
KK\) and \( KK\) corepresent Corti\~nas and Thom's diffeotopy \(K\)-theory. We use the Chern character to show that up to a suitable Schatten-class stabilisation, the complexified Chern character from the diffeotopy \(K\)-theory (resp. \(K\)-homology) of a smooth manifold to the compactly supported cohomology (resp. locally finite homology) of the manifold is an isomorphism.
paper.title: Bivariant $K$-theory for bornological algebras

paper.abstract: We construct a compact simply connected eight-manifold with holonomy Spin(7) and a triple Massey product of degrees $(3,2,2)$ that does not contain zero. The manifold is a resolution of a flat orbifold. Joyce's gluing theorem gives it a torsion-free Spin(7) structure. The resolution map factors through a quotient of $Y\times S^1$, where $Y$ is Mart\'in-Merch\'an's nonformal $G_2$ manifold. The map to this quotient has degree one, so pullback preserves a nonzero Massey pairing. On the resolution the detecting degree-two class annihilates the full indeterminacy. Simple connectivity and nonformality imply full Spin(7) holonomy. The manifold has $(b_2,b_3,b_4^+,b_4^-)=(22,10,91,27)$.
paper.title: A compact nonformal manifold with holonomy Spin(7)

paper.abstract:
We give an explicit example, in the stable homotopy groups of spheres, of a fourfold Toda bracket that is not defined although both of its threefold subbrackets contain zero. Namely, $0\in\langle
u^2,2,\eta^2angle$ and $0\in\langle 2,\eta^2,
uangle$, but $\langle
u^2,2,\eta^2,
uangle$ has no defining system in the sense of Kochman. This answers a question of Isaksen. The computational input consists only of relations from Toda's book, together with an explicit choice of null-homotopies. The same holds, in the sense of Walker, for the unstable quadruple $(
u_n^2,2\iota_{n+6},\eta_{n+6}^2,
u_{n+8})$ for every $n\ge10$. Moreover, for $n\ge10$, even Cohen's fourfold bracket of this quadruple is empty.
paper.title: A fourfold Toda bracket that is not defined, although both threefold subbrackets contain zero

paper.abstract: In this paper, we determine the second integral homology $H_2(J_n;\mathbb{Z})$ of cactus groups $J_n$. We first use Hopf's formula and Pontryagin products to obtain a smaller generating set of $H_2(J_n;\mathbb{Z})$. We then construct a detecting homomorphism to prove that these generators are linearly independent and hence form an explicit basis.
paper.title: Explicit Bases for the Second Integral Homology of Cactus Groups

paper.abstract: We construct the Grandis model structure on directed spaces with $\Delta$-generated underlying spaces and on the full subcategory of $\Delta$-Hausdorff objects. In either setting the model structure is left proper, and its weak equivalences are precisely the maps that induce equivalences of fundamental categories in the sense of Grandis. The fundamental category functor preserves all small homotopy colimits with values in the folk model structure on small categories. For a union of two induced directed subspaces, the union square is a homotopy pushout precisely when Grandis's categorical pushout formula holds. His covering theorem gives this conclusion whenever the interiors of the two subspaces cover the space.
paper.title: Homotopical interpretation of directed Van Kampen

paper.abstract: Gromov conjectured that the macroscopic dimension of the universal cover of a closed $n$-manifold of positive scalar curvature is at most $n-2$. Gromov's conjecture holds for a closed spin manifold of dimension $n\geq 5$, provided that its fundamental group has property $(*)_m$, i.e., its classifying space is stably homotopy equivalent to a wedge of Moore spaces. We prove property $(*)_m$ for a large class of groups, including for instance the fundamental groups of closed hyperbolic $3$-manifolds, the commutator subgroups of right-angled Coxeter groups with low-dimensional nerves, pure braid groups, and many graph products thereof. As an additional application of independent interest, we show that there are finite-index subgroups of right-angled Artin groups that do not have property $(*)_m$ and can have arbitrary torsion in their (co)homology in any degree.
paper.title: Moore spaces, polyhedral products, and positive scalar curvature

paper.abstract: We prove a mod-$ p $ divisibility result for indices of elliptic operators assuming a smooth action by a finite $ p $-group on the base manifold of dimension $ n\le 2(p-1) $ with no stationary points and which lifts equivariantly to the operator bundles. We show as one consequence that if such manifolds are spin or stably almost complex, with the group action lifting to the relevant structure, then their class in the relevant bordism theory modulo $ p $ is fully determined by one genus, and indeed vanishes for $ n<2(p-1) $. We show as another consequence that there exists no closed connected $ 24 $-dimensional spin manifold $ M $ satisfying $ {\hat{A}(M)=1}, {\hat{A}(M;T_\mathbb{C}M)=0} $, and for which there exists a smooth non-trivial action by the monster group, resolving a question of Hirzebruch.
paper.title: On p-Group Actions and Index Divisibilities

paper.abstract:
Persistent homology provides a framework for studying the evolution of topological features across filtered spaces. While persistence diagrams give discrete invariants that record the birth and death of homological features, they do not directly encode analytic or geometric structure associated to persistence modules. This paper develops a spectral framework for persistent homology by introducing and studying a Laplace operator on the M\"obius chain complex, called the M\"obius homology Laplacian.
  M\"obius homology categorifies M\"obius inversion for persistence modules by replacing integer-valued data with vector-space-valued chain complexes. By equipping these chain complexes with inner products, we define a Laplace operator on the M\"obius chain complex whose kernel provides canonical cycle representatives for the associated M\"obius homology space. We analyze the spectral properties of this operator in two primary settings: one-parameter persistence modules and birth-death modules arising from filtrations of simplicial complexes. For one-parameter modules, we completely characterize the eigenvalues of the degree-one M\"obius homology Laplacian. For birth-death modules, we show that the trace and determinant of the degree-zero M\"obius homology Laplacian reflect the combinatorial structure of the persistence diagram.
paper.title: The M\"obius Homology Laplacian for Persistence Modules

paper.abstract: The Seifert--van Kampen theorem computes the fundamental group of a space from an open cover by two path-connected subspaces, provided their intersection is path-connected. This article gives a self-contained account of the theorem, explains its universal-property formulation as a pushout in the category of groups, and derives several standard computations. Particular attention is paid to base points, the role of path-connectedness, and the passage from a topological decomposition to a group presentation. The purpose is expository: the results are classical, and no claim of a new theorem is made.
paper.title: The Seifert--van Kampen Theorem

paper.abstract: Davis and Januszkiewicz proved that the facets of a simple $n$-polytope $P$ which is the orbit space of a small cover can be properly coloured by $2^{n}-1$ colours. The bound is sharp for $n=2$, it is not sharp for $n=3$ by the Four Color Theorem, and it was shown to be sharp for $n=4$ by the first author. We show that it is sharp for every $n\geq4$. The polytope is obtained from the dual of the cyclic polytope $C^{n}(2^{n}-1)$ by truncations of faces of codimension at least $3$. The resolution works over an arbitrary field and gives the sharp bound $(q^{n}-1)/(q-1)$ over the field with $q$ elements. More generally, every simple $n$-polytope whose facets can be properly coloured by $k\leq2^{n}-1$ colours becomes, after truncations of faces of codimension at least $3$, the orbit polytope of a small cover with the same chromatic number $k$. We also construct, for every $n\geq4$, a simple $n$-polytope with $\chi=2^{n}-1$ which is the orbit space of both a small cover and a quasitoric manifold, and in the oriented case we obtain the sharp bound $2^{n-1}$ for every $n\geq4$.
paper.title: Upper bound $2^{n}-1$ for chromatic number of orbit polytope of a small cover is attained for every $n\geq4$

paper.abstract: We study the Balmer spectrum of the small derived category of permutation modules of a finite group over a commutative Noetherian ring. In this generality, we obtain a set-theoretic description of the spectrum. Under certain mild additional assumptions on the base ring, we describe its topology by reducing the problem first to the modular locus and then to the case of elementary abelian groups. Furthermore, we introduce a twisted cohomology ring in this context, which allows us to realize the spectrum, in the case of elementary abelian $p$-groups, as a Dirac scheme. This extends recent work of Balmer and Gallauer from the setting of ground fields to the more general setting of commutative Noetherian rings.
paper.title: The Balmer spectrum of integral permutation modules

paper.abstract: In 1977 Katz asked for an explicit lower bound on the $p$-adic valuation of $(D^nf)(0)$, where $D$ is the normalized invariant derivation of a one-parameter formal group of finite height $h$ over a ring of $p$-adic integers and $f$ is a power series with integral coefficients. He answered the question at height two, for functions whose translates by the points of order $p$ sum to zero, with the bound $\lfloor np/(p^2-1)\rfloor$. For Lubin--Tate groups over unramified bases, results of Bannai and Kobayashi give the bound $c_hn-(h-1)$, where $c_h=\frac1{p-1}-\frac1{p^h-1}$. We prove this bound for every one-dimensional formal group whose multiplication by $p$ is divisible by $p$ below degree $p^h$, over any $p$-torsion-free $\mathbb Z_{(p)}$-algebra and for every integral $f$, together with the bound $\sum_{h\nmid j}\lfloor n/p^j\rfloor$. The slope $c_h$, the constant $h-1$, and the second bound at the powers of $p$ cannot be improved. At height two it follows that Katz's bound holds for every integral function except at the orders divisible by $p^2-1$, where it can fail by one, and it does fail at the first of them. Over a ramified base the hypothesis cannot be weakened to the height of the special fibre, while an action of the Teichmüller roots of unity restores it. For the Cartier dual of the Honda formal group of height $h$ we construct an integral model whose $h-1$ coordinate directions have the sharp slopes $p^i/(p^h-1)$, which add up to $c_h$, each with the optimal constant $1$. The height-two case is the local exponent in the second step of the timeline in Alpöge's note on the Riemann hypothesis, where the bound is stated with a logarithmic loss; for integral functions on the formal group the loss is the constant $1$. The results and their proofs were produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode). They were checked by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high and at effort max; the text was written by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max and edited by Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max. No human has checked them.
paper.title: Divisibility of invariant derivatives on formal groups of every height, on a question of Katz

paper.abstract: What is the shape of the space of all mathematical universes? We take classifying toposes whose points are elementary toposes or models of set theory, and look at their geometry. The space of all toposes is contractible, yet its open parts contain every countable homotopy type: spheres and tori live among mathematical universes. Set theory has a genuine hole, built from two constructibility degrees that no definition can tell apart, and arithmetic cannot see it.
paper.title: The shape of mathematical universes

paper.abstract: We prove completeness of the convex uniform 5-polytope list, conditional on the cited lower-dimensional classifications, the written reductions and the certificate checkers. Its members are Wythoff's constructions of types $A_5$, $B_5$, $D_5$, prisms over uniform 4-polytopes, and products of regular polygons with uniform polyhedra. Conway and Guy announced the four-dimensional classification; Möller gave a complete computer-assisted proof. We extend these neighborhood and radius methods to dimension five. Coxeter's and Johnson's constructions supply the known families. Unbounded polygon sizes require products, forced by neighbor distances and prism cells. Lean checks a conditional implication from explicit premises.
paper.title: The convex uniform 5-polytopes: a computer-assisted classification

paper.abstract: For ten distinct points on the unit sphere, we prove that the bicapped square antiprism uniquely minimizes Coulomb energy, up to orthogonal transformations and relabeling. We build on the Lean proof directed by Aravind Karthigeyan of the tricapped trigonal prism's nine-point optimality and uniqueness. We use the three-point positivity method of Bachoc and Vallentin and of Cohn and Woo. A three-point semidefinite bound confines every competitor of no greater energy to short intervals around the candidate's inner products. Gram-determinant tests determine their assignment to pairs; orthogonal alignment and a quantitative local energy inequality then force congruence. The candidate's height is the unique critical point in a rational interval. We formalize the argument in Lean. This work has not yet been reviewed by experts. The proofs, the Lean formalization, the certificate checkers and the text were produced by AI models, working under the author's direction.
paper.title: The Thomson problem for N = 10

paper.abstract: This article confirms predictions made by Hopkins' chromatic splitting conjecture in stable homotopy theory. A consequence of our main theorem is that a certain map of $K(h-1)$-local $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-rings $\mathbb{S}_{K(h-1)}^{B\mathbb{Z}}\to L_{K(h-1)}\mathbb{S}_{K(h)}$ admits a retract, so long as $p-1$ does not divide $h-1$. If $h=2$ and $p$ is odd, we show this map is an isomorphism. We use methods from the theory of $p$-divisible groups and $p$-adic geometry. Along the way we prove an entirely new kind of "two-tower isomorphism," in analogy with Faltings' isomorphism between the Lubin--Tate and Drinfeld towers, which parametrizes $p$-divisible groups over characteristic $p$ perfectoid spaces with fixed generic fiber in terms of negative Banach--Colmez spaces. Using the two-tower isomorphism, we gain control over the continuous cohomology of the Morava stabilizer group $\mathbb{G}_h$ with coefficients in $\pi_*L_{K(h-1)}E_h$. To study the continuous action of $\mathbb{G}_h$ on $L_{K(h-1)} E_h$, it was necessary to develop the theory of solid Lubin--Tate spectra. Adapting Lurie's constructions, we attach a solid Lubin--Tate spectrum to $p$-divisible groups over a broad class of solid rings in characteristic $p$.
paper.title: On the chromatic splitting conjecture in coheight $1$

paper.abstract:
This article develops a second stage of an argument begun in 2013, revisiting Alain Badiou's use of topos theory in Being and Event and Logics of Worlds. The previous article diagnosed Badiou's reduction of topos theory to its atomistic, localic form as the scientific scapegoat in his attack on 'democratic materialism'. Now I ask what follows when this logicist illusion is dispelled and the categorical alternative is taken seriously, particularly with respect to forcing, semantic expression, and mathematical subjectification that constitute the key elements of Badiou's earlier work.
  I thus reconstruct Badiou's own arguments in a corrected form, while transferring them to a categorical framework. The aim is not to introduce new mathematical results, but to identify what is conceptually lost through their reduction to set-theoretic formalism. In particular, I describe Cohen's forcing argument in the context of Grothendieck topoi and Kripke-Joyal semantics, thereby explicating the geometric structures implicit in Badiou's thinking.
  This reconstruction further brings into view a different way of understanding Badiou's concepts of subject, body, and change. Rather than treating a topos as merely a formal container for mathematical objects, I propose reading it as a body of mathematical expression, aligning with Johnstone's characterization of a topos as a 'universe of discourse'. At the same time, the geometrization of logic allows Badiou's own four-fold typology of change - when applied to topos theory itself as a mathematical 'event' - to be anchored to various historical definitions of a topos.
  In this way, the article bridges Badiou's two major works while clarifying how his own limited expression of mathematical formalism embodies his 'dialectical', ultimately singular concept of the event, and the way it clouds his philosophical understanding of locality and temporality.
paper.title: Bridging Badiou's Gaps: Topos Theory and the Bodies of Mathematical Expression

paper.abstract: We settle the Kneser-Tits problem over every field $k$ of (separable) cohomological dimension $\le 2$, thus resolving a conjecture of Gille. More precisely, for such a $k$ and a semisimple, simply connected $k$-group $G$ whose indecomposable factors over $k$ are isotropic, we show that $G(k)$ is generated by "elementary matrices" (the $k$-points of the unipotent radicals of the parabolic $k$-subgroups of $G$), in other words, that $K_1^G(k) \cong 1$. In fact, we show this vanishing already when $k$ has separable $p$-dimension $\le 2$ in the sense of Gille with respect to a subset of the torsion primes $p$ of $G$, and we reinterpret the separable $p$-dimension itself via syntomic cohomology. To approach those $G$ that escape the net of previously known cases, for an inclusion of reductive $k$-groups $M \subset L$, we develop a new method based on the Rost invariant for transferring $R$-equivalence on $L/M$ to $R$-equivalence on $L$. To find homogeneous spaces to which our method fruitfully applies, we use the theories of prehomogeneous vector spaces and of special symplectic representations: concretely, for a $32$-dimensional half-spin representation $V$, we argue that the vectors in its unique open orbit $O \subset V$ admit unique up to interchange decompositions into sums of two pure spinors, and show that various double covers of $O$ built from such decompositions are rational varieties over any base field.
paper.title: Kneser-Tits over fields of cohomological dimension $\le 2$ (with an appendix by Alexis Bouthier and Federico Scavia)

paper.abstract: In topological data analysis, path homology accounts for directed graph while combinatorial Laplacian extends homology groups to spectral theory. However, these approaches are built on a boundary operator with condition $\partial^2=0$. Mayer homology replaces this condition with $N$-nilpotent boundary map $\partial^N=0$. By using the primitive $N$-th root of unity in the boundary operator, it relates each degree $n$ to the degrees $n-q$ and $n+N-q$. This work introduces persistent Mayer path homology. We show that Mayer path homology is functorial for strict digraph maps, which gives persistent Mayer path homology for filtered digraphs, and prove that its barcodes are stable under perturbations. For $N=3$ we derive formulas that reduce $\beta_0^{3,1}$ and $\beta_2^{3,2}$ to the classes of vertices identified by squares and the rank of a small matrix indexed by triangles. We also introduce the Mayer path Laplacian and its persistence theory, prove that their kernels recover (persistent) Mayer path homology, show that they distinguish digraphs with the same Mayer path Betti numbers, and prove a stability bound for the eigenvalues of the persistent up-Laplacian. We demonstrate that persistent Mayer path homology detects the formation of feed-forward loops, whose formation is not detected by ordinary path homology. In an application to cucurbit[7]uril, filtered by an interatomic distance normalized by van der Waals radii, Mayer path homology separates contacts that only close cycles from contacts that close feed-forward triangles, and changes at almost four times as many filtration values as path homology after the bonded framework is formed.
paper.title: Persistent Mayer Path Homology and Mayer Path Laplacian

paper.abstract:
A representation theorem is proved for spectral systems indexed by the lattice of down-sets of a finite poset P. Over an arbitrary associative ring, every excisive, homotopy-exact chain system of differential modules is isomorphic to the chain system of a projective P-graded differential module with a single upper-triangular differential. Consequently, every Cartan-Eilenberg system that is excisive and chain generated, together with its spectral system, admits such a differential model. An example over Z/4 shows that chain generation cannot be dropped. A chain system over Z/8 with short exact rows, whose maps commute only up to homotopy, shows that homotopy-exactness cannot be weakened to distinguished triangles in the derived category.
  Under finiteness conditions the model is finitely generated. The proof combines a derived horseshoe lemma with induction over the lattice, and yields a short proof and extension of Franzosa's connection matrix theory.
paper.title: Representations of spectral systems over finite distributive lattices

paper.abstract: For the induced complex on primitive integer pairs in a triangular lattice, we identify first homology with interior components of a half-scale midpoint bond graph. Its complementary planar dual has the visible-site graph as its line graph, giving a bijection between finite visible islands and bounded nonsingleton dual faces. In particular the hole density $h$ is a local Euler-product term plus the island density $b_0$: $h=3J_2-2J_3-J_1+b_0$, with $J_j=\prod_p(1-j/p^2)$. Each odd prime produces a matching, two primes produce a small forest, and diameter exclusion bounds cycle birth. We refine the bounds by retaining the actual earlier prime sieve at each step. A computer-assisted certificate, including a nonnegative coverage recurrence for islands, yields $0.10917978<h<0.10923225$. A separate length-six finite-path CRT method gives $h>0.10914952$, still below the island certificate, and an exact decomposition distinguishes old-component chords from cycles born among new cross-component bonds. Assuming the random-coprime nonpercolation theorem of Le Fourn--Liu--Martineau, the relative cycle increment of a new prime converges to a conditional connection probability. The planar correspondences, density existence, and numerical bounds do not require this probabilistic input.
paper.title: Holes and Islands of Visible Points on the Triangular Lattice: Midpoint Bond Graphs and Prime-Sieve Bounds

paper.abstract: The class $x_{153,3}$ lies in stable degree $153$ and filtration $3$ on the algebraic starting page of the $3$-primary Adams--Novikov spectral sequence of the sphere. We show that it survives and begins a family with period $144$, answering both parts of a question of Carrick and Davies. A comparison with periodic topological modular forms and a bound on the possible differential targets prove permanence. A divisibility calculation for the mod-$3$ Moore spectrum supplies a lift to a finite spectrum with a degree-$144$ self-map. The resulting iterates have nonzero image in the height-two detector of Carrick and Davies.
paper.title: Permanence and $144$-periodicity of $x_{153,3}$ in the stable stems at the prime three

paper.abstract: We prove that the homology of symplectic groups with Steinberg module coefficients forms a comodule algebra over the homology of general linear groups with Steinberg module coefficients. We prove a freeness-type result for comodule algebras. We deduce new lower bounds for the high-dimensional cohomology of symplectic groups of number rings and their congruence subgroups.
paper.title: Comodule algebras and the cohomology of symplectic groups

paper.abstract: Let $R$ be a perfect $\mathbb F_p$-algebra or a nonzero $p$-torsionfree perfectoid ring and $p$ be an arbitrary prime number. We compute the $RO(C_{p^n})$-graded Tambara functor of $\operatorname{THH}(R;\mathbb Z_p)$ for every $n\ge0$, including all homotopy groups, products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions and norms. We also compute genuine cyclotomic restriction.
paper.title: The $RO(C_{p^n})$-graded Tambara functor of perfectoid THH

paper.abstract: We construct a homotopy coherent product structure extending the Chas-Sullivan product on chains of the free loop space of a manifold. Our construction uses the framework of Morse homology with DG coefficients and perturbed Morse gradient trees. We define an operad given by moduli spaces of Morse gradient trees with a twisted differential. This Morse tree operad receives a map from a suspended A$\infty$-operad and in turn acts on Morse homology with DG coefficients associated to a fibration over a manifold with a fibrewise monoidal structure.
paper.title: An A $\infty$ -algebra structure for enriched Morse complexes

paper.abstract: We show that the rational compactly supported cohomology of the moduli space $\mathcal{A} = \bigsqcup_{g \geq 0} \mathcal{A}_g$ of principally polarized abelian varieties is free as a bigraded module over the Hopf algebra formed by its weight-zero subspace. The action arises from a symplectic analog of the Waldhausen $S$-construction. This structure yields new lower bounds for Betti numbers and the dimensions of the graded pieces of the weight filtration on the cohomology of $\mathcal{A}_g$. In particular, $\dim H_c^{2g + k}(\mathcal{A}_g)$ grows at least exponentially with $g$ for every nonnegative $k \neq 1, 3$. We also give conjectural descriptions of the full mixed Hodge structures in genera four and five, and of mixed Tate subquotients of $H_c^{2g}(\mathcal{A}_g)$ associated with shuffle algebras and multiple zeta values in every genus.
paper.title: A Hopf algebra action on the cohomology of moduli of abelian varieties

paper.abstract: We introduce the determinant Massey product, a secondary operation on the cohomology of commutative dg algebras which is reminiscent of the classical Massey product. We prove some of the elementary properties of this product, compute several examples, and relate them to classical and matric Massey products. When 2 is invertible, a determinant Massey product is a matric Massey product, but over $\mathbb F_2$, it is not. In this case, we produce a finite-dimensional cdga whose Harrison cohomology does not inject into its Hochschild cohomology, and a divided powers algebra which is formal as an associative dg algebra, but not as a commutative one, with an explicit determinant Massey product witnessing the failure. Over $\mathbb Q$, we use determinant Massey products to construct a simply-connected coformal space with Koszul cohomology ring and vanishing ordinary Massey products of all orders, which is not formal.
paper.title: Determinant Massey products

paper.abstract:
Let $X$ be a connected finite-type CW-complex with a map to the circle that is surjective on fundamental groups. If $X$ is formal, the algebraic monodromy of the associated infinite cyclic cover has no Jordan block of size greater than one at the eigenvalue 1, over the rationals; if the $d$-fold cyclic cover of $X$ along the map is formal, the same holds at every $d$-th root of unity. We study how formality of finite abelian covers and Jordan blocks of the monodromy constrain each other. We call $X$ Alexander formal if there are no such blocks at any root of unity, rationally, nor at the eigenvalue 1 modulo any prime $p$. Each condition amounts to the vanishing of certain Massey products along the class of the map; together they say that the rational cochains of every finite cyclic cover along the map, and the mod-$p$ cochains of $X$, are formal as DG modules over the cohomology of the circle. For the complement of a central hyperplane arrangement, with its Milnor fibration, Alexander formality holds exactly when the numbers of hyperplanes in its irreducible factors have no common divisor greater than 1; so the complement of an irreducible arrangement of two or more hyperplanes is never Alexander formal, although it is formal.
  On the side of covers, we show that a CDGA graded by an abelian group, over a field of characteristic zero in which the characters of the group separate its points, is formal if and only if it is formal as a graded CDGA. Consequently, the strong formality of Kohno and Pajitnov implies formality of every finite abelian cover of $X$; the converse fails, through a Jordan block at an eigenvalue of infinite order, which no finite cover detects. Modulo $p$, eigenvalues of $p$-power order collide with 1, producing Jordan blocks that strong formality allows. The two conditions are incomparable; all four resulting classes contain arrangement complements.
paper.title: Formality of finite abelian covers and Jordan blocks of the monodromy

paper.abstract: Persistence diagrams are widely used in topological data analysis to summarize topological and geometric structure in data. We study nonparametric regression where inputs are persistence diagrams and outputs are real-valued. Using kernel-based local averaging estimators defined directly over diagram space with Wasserstein distance, we establish consistency and derive bounds on the rate of convergence under suitable assumptions in the $L^2$-theory. We also present computational experiments that demonstrate strong performance of the proposed estimator, particularly in low data regimes.
paper.title: Kernel Regression using Persistence Diagrams

paper.abstract: We show that Morse representations can be algebraically described by spectral systems, a notion introduced by B. Matschke for poset-filtered chain complexes. This provides an algebraic alternative to connection matrices and yields algebraic invariants via R-modules over an arbitrary ring R. This approach applies in particular to Conley index theory for semi-flows. We discuss the theory of spectral systems and, as an application to dynamical systems, explain the relation to R. Franzosa's theory of connection matrices. In this context we introduce the concept of a spectral net. In contrast to traditional spectral sequences, spectral nets over a lattice display a rich network of (higher) differentials. In the application to dynamical systems these differentials provide information about connecting orbits.
paper.title: Lattice-ordered Spectral Systems for Morse Representations

paper.abstract: We prove that all coefficients of the Ehrhart polynomial of an integral polypositroid are strictly positive. In particular, this proves the positroid conjecture of Ferroni, Jochemko and Schröter. More generally, inclusion of integral polypositroids in a common cyclic order implies coefficientwise comparison of their Ehrhart polynomials. Hence the hypersimplex dominates every positroid of the same rank and size. We express each coefficient as a sum of relative face volumes multiplied by explicit nonnegative rational weights. The weights count linear extensions and specialize, for hypersimplices, to Ferroni's formula involving weighted Lah and Eulerian numbers. In the appendix we exhibit two representable matroids whose quartic Ehrhart coefficients exceed those of the hypersimplices of the same rank and size.
paper.title: Ehrhart positivity for polypositroids

paper.abstract:
$A_\infty$-algebras over a commutative ring $R$ are generalizations of $R$-algebras in which multiplication is only associative up to higher homotopies. Similarly, $A_\infty$-categories over $R$ are generalizations of $R$-linear categories in which composition of morphisms is only associative up to higher homotopies. They are important in the definition of Fukaya categories in Symplectic Geometry, and in other areas of mathematics.
  By $\infty$-categories we mean quasicategories, a class of simplicial sets which are a model for $(\infty,1)$-categories, used in the work of Jacob Lurie.
  We define and study $\infty$-categories of $A_\infty$-algebras and $A_\infty$-categories. Our approach is unusual in that rather than defining them by localization, we construct our $\infty$-categories completely explicitly as simplicial sets.
  Our $\infty$-categories are intended for applications to Fukaya categories in Symplectic Geometry. Given a suitable symplectic manifold $(X,\omega)$, one should construct its Fukaya category ${\mathscr F}(X,\omega)$, a (filtered) $A_\infty$-category, and its derived Fukaya category $D^b{\mathscr F}(X,\omega)$, a triangulated category (or better, a stable $\infty$-category). Typically ${\mathscr F}(X,\omega)$ depends on many arbitrary choices. Our $\infty$-categories give a clean way to explain in what sense ${\mathscr F}(X,\omega)$ and $D^b{\mathscr F}(X,\omega)$ are independent of these choices.
paper.title: An $\infty$-category approach to $A_\infty$-algebras and $A_\infty$-categories

paper.abstract: We construct a map of filtered spectra inducing a map from the Atiyah--Hirzebruch spectral sequence (AHSS) to the Baker--Lazarev Adams spectral sequence of a $\mathit{ko}$-module $M$. Using this and a theorem of Bruner--Rognes, we construct a hastened Adams spectral sequence (HASS) for the Postnikov truncations of $\mathit{ko}$ and the connective Adams summand. Then, motivated by questions in quantum field theory, topological phases of matter, and tensor category theory, we apply the HASS to supercohomology, the cohomology theory $I_{\mathbb{C}^\times}(\tau_{\le 2}\mathit{ko})$, and observe that in examples of interest it is easier to calculate with than either the AHSS or the usual Adams spectral sequence. We include a User's Guide to the HASS and several worked examples, as well as hastened Adams charts for many commonly encountered $\mathcal{A}(1)$-modules.
paper.title: An Atiyah--Hirzebruch to Adams map and the hastened Adams spectral sequence for supercohomology

paper.abstract: This paper develops a deformation theory for stable $(\infty,n)$-categories for $n > 1$. We introduce the framework of complete $t$-structured stable presentable $(\infty,n)$-categories. Within this setting, we establish a higher categorified Koszul duality among complete $t$-structured presentable $(\infty,n)$-categories. Using this duality, we develop the deformation theory. We prove that the deformation problem for such categories is a well-behaved formal moduli problem determined by Hochschild cohomology, and we deduce the corresponding obstruction theory. Finally, we apply our results to sheaves of categories on perfect stacks.
paper.title: Categorified Koszul duality and deformation theory of higher categories

paper.abstract: Let $R$ be an $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-ring spectrum of height $m$. The chromatic redshift theorem implies that its $n$-fold iterated algebraic $K$-theory $K^{(n)}(R)$ has height $m+n$. Moreover, there is a natural map $K^{(n)}(R)\to (T^n\otimes R)^{hT^n}$, where $T^n\otimes R$ denotes the $n$-fold iterated topological Hochschild homology. Hence it is natural to ask whether the target also has height $m+n$. Although this fails in general, we prove that it holds whenever $R$ is connective and $m\geq1$. Our proof is based on an iterative calculation using Wilson spaces and relative topological Hochschild homology. As an application, we determine the support of the $T^n$-homotopy fixed points of $n$-fold iterated topological Hochschild homology of $\mathrm{BP}\langle m\rangle$ for $n=2,3$ with $\mathrm{BP}\langle m\rangle$ equipped with any $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}$-form.
paper.title: Chromatic heights of homotopy fixed points of iterated topological Hochschild homology of connective spectra

paper.abstract:
Let $M$ be a closed $d$-dimensional smooth manifold and $X:\Delta^{op}\rightarrow\operatorname{Fin}$ a finite simplicial set whose geometric realization is homeomorphic to $M$. Given the $\infty$-category $\mathcal{D}\mathrm{isk}_{/M}$ of disks embedded in $M$ and the path components functor $\pi_0:\mathcal{D}\mathrm{isk}_{/M}\rightarrow\operatorname{Fin}$, we construct a cofinal functor $\Gamma_X:\Delta^{op}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}\mathrm{isk}_{/M}$ such that $X=\pi_0\circ\Gamma_X$.
  This result provides an alternative construction of a simplicial model developed by Boavida de Brito, Lambrechts, Pryor and Songhafouo Tsopm\'en\'e to compute the space-valued presheaf $\operatorname{Emb}(-,M):\mathcal{D}\mathrm{isk}^{op}\rightarrow\mathcal{S}$. We also extend the result to manifolds with a $G$-structure and discuss applications to manifold calculus, factorization homology, and a possible generalization to manifolds with boundary.
paper.title: A simplicial model for manifold calculus through the configuration category

paper.abstract: Diffeological non-Abelian Hodge theory motivates the study of $C^r$ families of Higgs bundles and flat bundles for finite $r$. In this article, we provide a uniform language for treating moduli stacks parametrizing such objects in terms of diffeology. More specifically, we develop a theory of stacks presentable by diffeological groupoids over the site of $C^r$ manifolds for arbitrary $r$. As an application, we construct moduli stacks over the sites of $C^r$ manifolds parametrizing $C^r$ vector bundles over a smooth manifold, and $C^r$ families of Higgs bundles and of flat bundles over a complex manifold. We also construct $C^r$ versions of the non-Abelian Hodge filtration stack, interpolating between Higgs bundles and flat bundles through $\lambda$--connections. We show that all these stacks are presentable by diffeological groupoids. Finally, we construct moduli stacks parametrizing $C^r$ families of $\Delta^n$--shaped diagrams of these objects, and show that they assemble into simplicial stacks whose levels are all presentable by diffeological groupoids.
paper.title: Finite regularity moduli stacks through diffeology

paper.abstract: We introduce the notion of semi-exact functors between abelian categories, which are characterised by either preserving or breaking exactness of sequences. We prove semi-exact functors are always exact with respect to a canonically determined exact structure. For a symmetric tensor category $\Cs$, we define a support theory by considering all $\Bbbk$-linear symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors $\mathscr{C}\to\operatorname{Ver}_{p^\infty}$ up to equivalence, and conjecture that it agrees with the Balmer spectrum of the stable category when $\mathscr{C}$ is finite. We prove a weak form of this conjecture and other results for Tannakian categories and in characteristic 0. Critical to the positive characteristic case is a functor constructed by Coulembier and Flake who were interested in higher Frobenius functors. We show that their construction, which relies on the theory of abelian envelopes, gives a natural source for semi-exact functors, and at least in the Tannakian setting gives all $\Bbbk$-linear, symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors.
paper.title: Semi-exact functors and the conjecture of Coulembier and Flake

paper.abstract: Following Botvinnik--Rosenberg \cite{BotvinnikRosenberg2023}, we define fibered-boundary bordism, introduce sphere-bundle bordism, and prove an exact sequence relating them to ordinary bordism. The sequence also holds when all sphere fibers are required to be non-$D^r$-bounding. Following Debray--Ye--Yu \cite{DebrayYeYu2026}, we define characteristic cycles with a chosen complement structure trivializing a characteristic class. For the GM and $\mathrm{KT}^{\pm}$ cases, deleting tubular neighborhoods and identifying sphere-bundle structures with determinant-twisted base structures give a characteristic exact sequence. This proves the bordism-group consequence of the DYY conjecture for our definitions, without constructing the conjectured map of spectra.
paper.title: A Geometric Characteristic Long Exact Sequence for Codimension-Two Spin and Pin-plus/minus Bordism

paper.abstract: Given a simplicial set $X$, let $\operatorname{B}({X})$ denote its poset of nondegenerate simplices. We define a natural stratification $\left\vert{X}\right\vert\rightarrow\operatorname{B}({X})$. When $X$ is locally finite, we prove that this stratification is conical. Moreover, if $X$ is finite, we prove that the exit path category $\operatorname{Exit}^{\operatorname{B}({X})}(\left\vert{X}\right\vert)$ satisfies the geometric realization formula $\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\limits_{\sigma:\Delta[p]\rightarrow X} \operatorname{Exit}^{\operatorname{B}({p})}(\Delta^p)\simeq\operatorname{Exit}^{\operatorname{B}({X})}(\left\vert{X}\right\vert)$ where the colimit is indexed by the category of simplices of $X$.
paper.title: A stratified version of geometric realizations

paper.abstract: We show that, after attaching a subcritical handle to $T^*\bP^2$ to obtain a manifold $M$, the integral wrapped Floer endomorphism algebra of a cotangent fibre admits no spherical refinement for any choice of brane structure; this obstructs the existence of any wrapped Fukaya category for $M$ over the sphere spectrum. We further discuss some features of the resulting Weinstein eight-manifold $M$, which is homotopy equivalent to $S^4$.
paper.title: A Weinstein manifold without any spherical Fukaya category

paper.abstract: We prove the cosmetic crossing conjecture, Problem 1.58 in Kirby's list, and the generalized cosmetic crossing conjecture for every knot whose branched double cover is an L-space; in particular, both hold for all alternating and all quasi-alternating knots. We also prove the oriented knot complement conjecture, Problem 1.81(D), for all closed 3-manifolds with finite fundamental group, in particular for all lens spaces: in such a manifold, every knot whose exterior is irreducible and not a solid torus is determined by its complement. Both results rest on a monotonicity theorem for Heegaard Floer correction terms: if a knot in a rational homology sphere has an isotropic, nonzero homology class, then the sum of all correction terms strictly increases along its surgeries with coefficients -1/j relative to the rational longitude, so no nontrivial surgery yields the original oriented manifold. We also show that every purely cosmetic band surgery on a knot with an L-space branched double cover is weakly nugatory, which answers a question of Rogers for these knots.
paper.title: Cosmetic crossings and the knot complement problem

paper.abstract: Hypergraphs are the natural language for group interactions, and topological data analysis has given us several ways to look at them: simplicial and cell complexes, persistent homology, and sheaves. All of these treat a hyperedge as an unordered set. In this paper, we introduce a different and, to our knowledge, new viewpoint that comes from Grothendieck's theory of dessins d'enfants and, unlike these approaches, takes into account the order in which vertices appear in each hyperedge and hyperedges appear around each vertex. A dessin is a bipartite graph drawn on a closed orientable surface. Through Walsh's classical correspondence between hypermaps and bipartite maps, every hypergraph equipped with a cyclic order of incidences at each vertex and inside each hyperedge is a dessin, and therefore determines a surface with faces and a genus. We develop this idea for temporal hypergraphs and build the surface by replaying history: incidences are added in the order in which they occurred, and each new incidence is inserted into the cyclic orders built so far, next to the earlier incidence to which it is related. We prove that every insertion either grows the hypergraph without creating a cycle, closes a cycle locally by splitting a face, or closes it globally by adding a handle; the number of independent cycles equals the number of local plus handle events, and the genus equals the number of handle events. These counts give interpretable, size-controlled measures of how a temporal hypergraph's cycles organize on a surface as it grows. We apply our method to five Stack Exchange communities and show that it separates communities that standard statistics cannot tell apart and quantifies how much the real order of interactions matters. We further discuss what the surface viewpoint adds to existing higher-order network analysis and how it opens a path toward dessin-based learning on hypergraphs.
paper.title: Dessins d'Enfants as a Topological Lens on Temporal Hypergraphs

paper.abstract: In this paper, we address the construction of Eilenberg-MacLane coordinates (functions from datasets to Eilenberg-MacLane spaces $K(G,n)$) that encode nontrivial persistent cohomology classes in arbitrary dimensions $n$ and coefficient group $G$. The construction leverages the connecting homomorphism in the long exact sequence in \v{C}ech cohomology, from the short exact sequence of sheaves of continuous maps with values in $G$, $EG$ and $BG$. Crucially, the derivation is constructive: we give an explicit, recursive formula for preimages under the connecting homomorphism, which yields a constructive version of a classical cohomology vanishing theorem and, in turn, an algorithm for general Eilenberg-MacLane coordinates. We validate our approach through experiments on synthetic datasets, and present novel examples of $K(\mathbb{Z}/2, 2)$-coordinates not addressed in prior work.
paper.title: From Persistent Cohomology to Maps into Arbitrary Eilenberg-MacLane Spaces

paper.abstract:
We prove an explicit stability line for the homology $H_i(\mathrm{Hur}_n^c,\mathbb{Q})$ of any Hurwitz space associated to a finite rack $c$ depending only on its homology up to some finite $n$. Moreover, as the range of $n$ increases, the slope of the resulting stability line converges to the optimal slope. Thus, for any Hurwitz space, a finite computation will yield near-optimal bounds on secondary terms for the corresponding arithmetic statistics problem. Our theorem also applies more generally to higher order stability, Frobenius weights, and braided vector spaces.
  As a special case of our theorem, we can deduce stability lines depending only on when $H_0(\mathrm{Hur}^c_n,\mathbb{Q})$ stabilizes, which are sharp in some cases. We apply this to two families of Hurwitz spaces to obtain bounds on the secondary term for (1) the number of $S_d$-degree $d$ function fields with squarefree discriminant, and (2) Cohen-Lenstra moments.
paper.title: Optimal homological stability: bounding secondary terms of Cohen-Lenstra moments and $S_d$-fields over $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$

paper.abstract: We prove that every polyhedral product of disks and their boundary spheres that is a topological manifold admits a stably parallelizable smooth structure. We also show that if a moment-angle complex or a real moment-angle complex admits a smooth structure for which the coordinate action is smooth, then the link of every face of the underlying simplicial complex is a simplicial sphere, and every such smooth structure is stably parallelizable.
paper.title: Smooth structures on polyhedral products of disks and spheres

paper.abstract: By regarding the nerves of categories enriched over a monoidal poset as persistence simplicial sets, we investigate an upper bound of the interleaving distance in the homotopy category between the nerves in the sense of Lanary and Scoccola. In particular, it holds that the distance between the nerves for $r$-homotopy equivalent generalized metric spaces is less than or equal to the half of $r$. Moreover, a product on the cochain complex associated with a persistence simplicial set is introduced and related to the cup product on the magnitude cochain complex in the sense of Hepworth. As a consequence, the product gives the multiplicative structure to the cohomological magnitude-path spectral sequence (MPSS) whose first term is isomorphic to the magnitude cohomology ring. Furthermore, we discuss at which term the MPSS for a connected finite digraph collapses by using the interleaving of the enriched nerve of the digraph.
paper.title: Enriched nerves, interleaving distances and the multiplicative magnitude-path spectral sequence

paper.abstract: We refine the classical pro-homotopy type of the end of a manifold by recording the boundaries of a compact exhaustion together with the bordisms between them. We show that this assignment, the bordism-end, is functorial in embeddings, and independent of the choice of exhaustion. Its target is the free sequential colimit completion of the bordism $\infty$-category. Along the way of defining the bordism-end, we show that the category of all smooth $d$-dimensional manifolds and embeddings is formally obtained from the analogous category of compact manifolds. Through the formalism of the bordism-end, it follows that a manifold is diffeomorphic to the interior of a compact manifold if and only if its bordism-end is representable. Moreover, this formalism yields a fibre sequence relating the classifying spaces of the compactly supported diffeomorphism group of a manifold and its full diffeomorphism group, and a space of bordism-ends. Finally, we set up the pro-end functorially in embeddings, with target the cospan $\infty$-category of pro-spaces, and show that it factors through the bordism-end.
paper.title: A bordism perspective on ends of manifolds

paper.abstract: We develop a theory of infinitesimal gradings for $\mathbb{Z}/2$-graded $A_\infty$-categories and use it to detect Calabi--Yau dimensions of monotone Fukaya summands from quantum cohomology. The dimensions we find agree with predictions from Serre functors of Kuznetsov components, such as $2$ for Gushel--Mukai and Verra fourfolds and the fractional value $\frac{n-2}{n}$ for the symplectic Grassmannian $\operatorname{IG}(2,2n)$. An infinitesimal grading induces endomorphisms on cohomological morphism spaces, and we prove a straightening theorem that realizes its weights as an actual grading compatible with the $A_\infty$-structure. We use this grading to show that Dehn twists give faithful braid group representations in the symplectic mapping class groups of Gushel--Mukai and Verra fourfolds.
paper.title: Calabi--Yau dimensions of monotone Fukaya summands from infinitesimal gradings

paper.abstract: For a $p$-torsionfree $p$-quasisyntomic ring, we construct a fiber sequence relating the $p$-th Nygaard graded piece of absolute prismatic cohomology to the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex. The latter is an arithmetic analogue of the cotangent complex in which the differential of $p$ need not vanish. We also clarify the relationship between the regularity criterion proved by Mao using the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex and the regularity criterion established by Bhatt and Mathew using the Nygaard graded piece. This relationship was anticipated by Bhatt and Mathew.
paper.title: The Nygaard graded piece, the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex and regularity criteria

paper.abstract: We show that, for every $\infty$-topos $\mathcal{X}$, the profinite shape induces a canonical equivalence between the $\infty$-category of pro-objects in locally constant constructible sheaves of anima in $\mathcal{X}$ and the slice $\infty$-category of profinite anima over the profinite shape $\widehat{\Pi}_{\infty}(\mathcal{X})$. We deduce this profinite shape equivalence from the monodromy classification theorem by establishing a continuous version of the straightening-unstraightening equivalence for profinite anima. In addition, we explain how the monodromy classification theorem recovers its classical counterparts concerning locally constant sheaves of finite sets and of (abelian) groups.
paper.title: The profinite shape equivalence

paper.abstract: We propose a definition of associative log rings. The role of the commutative monoid is replaced by a variant of a crossed module whose source is a monoid, and we use the resulting group action to control the failure of commutativity. This extends the classical notion of a log ring, even in the commutative case. Natural examples include algebras of logarithmic differential operators. The definition lends itself to a canonical construction of a log enveloping algebra and hence of log bimodules, and we prove that the resulting second log Hochschild cohomology group classifies log square-zero extensions. Along the way, we complete the logarithmic analog of Quillen's classification of abelian group objects in augmented algebras: In exact augmented associative log rings, abelian group objects recover log bimodules. Our constructions enjoy animated analogs, and we develop the basic theory of associative animated log rings \emph{en route} to our classification of exact log square-zero extensions.
paper.title: Associative Log Rings and their Bimodules

paper.abstract: The maximal abelian cover of a connected graph is the quotient of its universal cover by the commutator subgroup of its fundamental group. We provide a complete classification of finite connected graphs with isomorphic maximal abelian covers. For trees or for connected graphs with at least two cycles, the cover determines the base up to isomorphism; in cycle rank one, it determines the primitive cyclic pattern of rooted trees attached to the unique cycle. We also characterize when every automorphism descends to the base and give an orbit-size criterion for splitting the canonical lift extension, answering two questions raised by Baez in 2026.
paper.title: Complete characterization of graphs with common maximal abelian cover

paper.abstract: Distance algebras were introduced by Asao and Ivanov to realize magnitude homology and cohomology of quasi-metric spaces as Tor- and Ext-groups respectively. Let $\Sigma_L$ be the distance algebra of the Hasse graph of a finite distributive lattice $L$, where the metric is given by the lengths of shortest paths in the graph. We show that $\Sigma_L$ is Gorenstein over any Gorenstein commutative noetherian ring $R$, and give bound of its self-injective dimension. The proof constructs, for each indecomposable (relative) injective module, a projective resolution that is in general non-minimal. When $R=\Bbbk$ is a field, we use algebraic Morse theory to reduce it to a minimal resolution, so that the Betti numbers can be obtained as the dimensions of homologies of certain order complexes. As a consequence, we show that the self-injective dimension of $\Sigma_L$ is the maximal Castelnuovo--Mumford regularity of certain Stanley--Reisner rings. We also show that the first two terms of these minimal resolutions are multiplicity-free, whereas arbitrarily large multiplicities occur in every higher degree. In the appendix, we include a more abstract formulation of the non-minimal projective resolution, namely, a simplicial replacement of a diagram of projective modules.
paper.title: Distance algebras of finite distributive lattices are Gorenstein

paper.abstract: We compute the $\Gamma$-Euler characteristic of a finite-dimensional representation of the compact torus $\mathbb{T}^k$ where $\Gamma$ is an arbitrary finitely presented group. We additionally compute the $\Gamma$-Euler characteristic of the unit sphere in such a representation as well as the corresponding symplectic quotient at a nonzero level of the moment map. In each case, the $\Gamma$-Euler characteristic is expressed in terms of the weight matrix for the representation as well as a description of the abelianization of $\Gamma$.
paper.title: Higher orbifold Euler characteristics of torus representations

paper.abstract: Let $\beta_1$ be the first 3-torsion class in the stable homotopy groups of spheres in even degree. Toda showed that $\beta_1^5 \neq 0$, whilst $\beta_1^6 = 0$. Shimomura generalised this to the 144-periodic family generated by $\beta_1$, written as $\{\beta_{1+9s}\}_{s\geq 0}$, and showed that any $5$-fold product $\prod_5 \beta_{1+9s} \neq 0$, whilst all 6-fold products $\prod_6 \beta_{1+9s} = 0$. In this article, we give a simple proof of these results as well as some generalisations to other 144-periodic families. Along the way, we also refine known detection results for these families. Our tools include BP-synthetic spectra, and the well-known Adams--Novikov spectral sequence for the spectrum of topological modular forms at the prime $3$ as well as its Adams operations.
paper.title: Revisiting the $\beta_1$-action on the 3-primary stable homotopy groups of spheres

paper.abstract:
To study derived defect topological quantum field theories, we construct an $(\infty,1)$-category of stratified bordisms and sketch its $(\infty,d)$-dimensional analogue.
  In the first chapters we develop a method for constructing symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories, inspired by Segal spaces but better suited to geometric inputs, which we call interval Segal spaces. Using this framework, we construct the $(\infty,1)$-category of $d$-dimensional smooth manifolds via smooth $\infty$-sheaves thereof, in an attempt to address fibrancy issues present in prior work on this subject. We further equip this category with a symmetric monoidal structure, compute its homotopy 1-category, and extend the construction to manifolds endowed with tangential structures, obtaining the interval Segal space of $d$-dimensional bordisms with tangential structure.
