  To model the stratifications supporting topological defects, we work with conically smooth stratified spaces, a suitably smooth framework for conical stratifications.
  We define stratified topological manifolds as stratified $\mathcal{B}$-manifolds for a suitable $(\infty,1)$-category of basics $\mathcal{B}$. Using these, we construct an interval Segal space whose objects are compact closed stratified topological $(d-1)$-manifolds and whose 1-morphisms are stratified $d$-dimensional bordisms, and we endow it with a symmetric monoidal structure. We also use tangential structures on conically smooth stratified spaces to formulate a notion of defect labels, aiming toward bordisms with labeled defects in the style of Carqueville et al.
  Finally, we sketch a higher-dimensional generalization of the interval category to a category of $d$-cubes for $d>1$, conjecturally presenting $(\infty,d)$-categories, and outline how stratified factorization homology may be used to produce derived stratified defect TQFTs.
paper.title: An $(\infty,1)$-category of conically smooth stratified bordisms

paper.abstract: Locally standard $T$-pseudomanifolds are singular analogues of quasitoric manifolds. In this paper, we study a certain class of four-dimensional locally standard $T^2$-pseudomanifolds over convex polygons. We establish an Orlik-Raymond type classification and study their ordinary and equivariant cohomology, as well as their intersection and equivariant intersection cohomology. We also introduce ring structures on middle-perversity intersection cohomology and equivariant intersection cohomology via change of perversity. We show that these rings can be described in terms of the cohomology and equivariant cohomology of associated nonsingular spaces, which are quasitoric manifolds or $S^4$. Furthermore, we give combinatorial descriptions of the equivariant cohomology and equivariant intersection cohomology in terms of labelled graphs.
paper.title: Equivariant intersection cohomology of some $4$-dimensional locally standard $T$-pseudomanifolds

paper.abstract: This paper studies the higher Chow groups of arbitrary finite type separated schemes using motivic homotopy theory, serving as a Borel-Moore counterpart to the $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant motivic cohomology of Bachmann-Elmanto-Morrow. We construct a filtration on the G-theory spectrum of a finite type separated scheme $X$, inducing an Atiyah-Hirzebruch style spectral sequence whose associated graded pieces are a complex computing the higher Chow groups of $X$. We prove that this complex is representable in the stable motivic homotopy category, and is a module over the $\mathbb{A}^1$-motivic complex, giving rise to an action of $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant motivic cohomology on the Bloch-Levine cycle complex. This generalizes some results of Bloch and Levine relating higher Chow groups and motivic cohomology to the case of schemes over an arbitrary base, and which need not be smooth or equidimensional.
paper.title: Motivic Borel-Moore Homology is Borel-Moore Motivic Homology

paper.abstract: Lurie's cobordism hypothesis classifies fully extended framed topological field theories valued in a symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-category $\mathcal{C}$ with duals by the $\infty$-groupoid $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{fd}}$ of fully dualisable objects. This classification results in an $O(n)$-action on $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{fd}}$, where $O(n)$ acts on the framed bordism category by change of framing. Lurie observed that for a connective spectrum, this action is ``a version of the classical $J$-homomorphism.'' We make this identification explicit: with respect to the right action of $O(n)$ on framings, the $O(n)$-action on the localisation $L(\mathrm{Bord}_n^{\mathrm{fr}}) \simeq S$ is precisely $\ominus J_n$, the inverse of the unstable $J$-homomorphism $J_n \colon O(n) \to \mathrm{GL}_1(S)$. The identification of the action with the unstable $J$-homomorphism in the setting of smooth stacks is due to Grady--Pavlov; we give an independent proof in Lurie's original formulation of the cobordism hypothesis, using the abstract Pontryagin--Thom construction. The sign (i.e.\ whether the action is $J_n$ or $\ominus J_n$) depends on the convention for the $O(n)$-action on framings, and is relevant for $\mathrm{pin}^\pm$ theories and hence for quantum systems with time-reversal symmetry. We compute the induced action on homotopy groups of the sphere spectrum in low degrees, yielding explicit invariants for invertible TFTs in dimensions $1$, $2$, and $3$, and connect these to the Kitaev chain, the framing anomaly, the spin-statistics theorem, and anomaly inflow. We recover the Galatius--Madsen--Tillmann--Weiss theorem as a consequence of the cobordism hypothesis and relate the homotopy fixed-point and mapping-spectrum perspectives on invertible TFTs via the duality between tangential and normal framings.
paper.title: The $J$-Homomorphism From Localising The Cobordism Hypothesis

paper.abstract: Let $g_x$ be the Balmer-Favi idempotent at a point $x$ of the spectrum of a rigidly-compactly generated tensor triangulated category. We study the equality $\operatorname{Cosupp}(g_x)=\operatorname{gen}(x)$ by expressing $g_x$ as a local dual. We prove the equality for the derived category of a Noetherian scheme and for the stable module category of a finite group scheme over a field of positive characteristic. For $E(n)$-local spectra we express the maps between distinct monochromatic layers of the sphere in terms of the chromatic fracture square. The height-two splitting gives the equality through height two at every prime. For a Noetherian local ring we characterize the Gorenstein property by the form of its closed-point idempotent.
paper.title: A Note on the Cosupport of Balmer-Favi Idempotents

paper.abstract: We develop toric geometry spectral algebraic geometry. In particular, we lift toric varieties to flat schemes over the sphere spectrum. Furthermore, we prove several rigidity and strictness results allowing us to define and produce strict group actions of flat algebraic tori. As an application, we give a construction of the Tate curve in spectral algebraic geometry. This approach lets us produce a lift of the Tate curve to $\mathbb{S}[[q]]$. We furthermore describe how to lift (arithmetic) toric stacks.
paper.title: A toric construction of the spectral Tate curve

paper.abstract:
In this article, we continue our study of equivariant symplectic capacities of open sets in a cotangent bundle defined via the Chiu-Tamarkin complex constructed from the microlocal theory of sheaves.
  The paper consists of two parts: 1) We develop the theory of $S^1$-equivariant Chiu-Tamarkin complex over complex-oriented ring spectra. 2) Applications of the theory to symplectic capacities: We show that a product formula for the capacities, whose Ekeland-Hofer capacities version is folklore since 1988, is not true via an (uncountable family of) counterexample(s). The counterexample (family) is the product of a concave toric domain of dimension $6$ ($2n\geq 6$) and a $2$-dimensional disk. We also prove a Weyl law of the capacities for all toric domains in dimension $2n$. The algebraic verification is based on a chain model for the Chiu-Tamarkin complex of all toric domains in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, which recovers Irie's conjectural chain model of $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology for star-shaped toric domains (defined only) in $\mathbb{R}^4$.
paper.title: Capacities from the Chiu-Tamarkin complex II: Product formula and toric domains

paper.abstract: We study the regular slice filtration of representation spheres $S^V\wedge H\underline{M}$. For every finite group $G$, we locate all slices in an explicit interval $[n(V),k(V)]$ and show that both endpoints occur. We introduce a \emph{defect vector} to measure a slice's failure. For the Klein four-group with $\underline{\mathbb F}_2$-coefficients, a balanced defect allows us to move $S^V\wedge H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ by certain $RO(G)$-graded cohomology classes to its $\dim V$-slice, which is again a representation sphere, while an odd defect obstructs any spherical slice. As an application, we obtain closed formulas for the bottom slice of $\Sigma^nH\underline{\mathbb{F}}_2$ for every $n$, recovering the computation of Guillou and Yarnall by a different method. Along the way, we determine the complete slice tower of $S^{\infty\alpha_i}\wedge H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ and consequently, the partial tower for $S^{n\alpha_i}\wedge H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$.
paper.title: Klein four slices of the representation suspensions of $H\underline{\mathbb{F}_2}$

paper.abstract:
One of the best known invariants of multi-parameter persistent homology is the rank invariant, which is subsumed by the generalized rank invariant (GRI), obtained by naturally extending its domain. M\"obius inversion of the GRI not only provides a compact encoding of this invariant but is also useful for clarifying its relationship with other invariants of multi-parameter persistent homology. However, M\"obius inversion of the GRI has been defined only under suitable finiteness conditions on its domain and support. This work studies the extent to which M\"obius inversion can be extended beyond these finiteness conditions. Namely, we formalize the notion of M\"obius invertibility, which captures when M\"obius inversion exists beyond these finiteness conditions, and investigate when the GRI is M\"obius invertible.
  A central result we establish is that M\"obius invertibility of the GRI is guaranteed for finitely presentable $d$-parameter persistence modules when $d\leq 2$, but may fail when $d>2$. Establishing this failure also corrects an error in the existing literature. In response to this higher-dimensional obstruction, we show that for finitely presentable $d$-parameter persistence modules, restricting the GRI to intervals subordinate to the finite grid supporting a minimal free presentation preserves its M\"obius inversion whenever the latter exists over all intervals. Since computing the GRI over all intervals in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is infeasible in practice, this result provides a principled justification for restricting the GRI to those intervals.
paper.title: M\"obius Invertibility of Rank Invariants

paper.abstract: In this paper, we study quasi-F-splitting from the viewpoint of non-commutative algebraic geometry. Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p. For a proper dg-category over k with a Serre functor, we define quasi-F^e-split heights for e\geq 1 by using finite topological restriction homology with coefficients in a shift of the Serre functor. Using the functoriality of polygonic topological Hochschild homology for laced categories due to Harpaz--Nikolaus--Saunier, we show that these heights are invariant under derived Morita equivalence. For a proper Gorenstein scheme of pure dimension over k, the height for e=1 of its dg-category of perfect complexes coincides with the quasi-F-split height in the sense of Yobuko. For a complete Noetherian Gorenstein local \(k\)-algebra with residue field k, the dg-category of perfect complexes supported at the closed point recovers the n-quasi-F^e-splitting of Tanaka--Witaszek--Yobuko for all n,e\geq 1. The proofs use the computation of the zeroth homotopy groups of TR with coefficients due to Dotto--Krause--Nikolaus--Patchkoria, Zariski descent, and Serre duality or local duality.
paper.title: Quasi-F-split heights and derived Morita invariance

paper.abstract: We study faithful Galois extensions in a presentably symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category $\mathscr{C}$ by a dualizable $\mathbb{E}_1$-group $G$. We prove that these extensions correspond to colimit-preserving symmetric monoidal functors from $\mathrm{An}^{\mathrm{B}G}$ to $\mathscr{C}$. Under suitable assumptions, we use this correspondence to construct a Galois pro-anima that classifies Galois extensions in $\mathscr{C}$. This generalizes the \'etale fundamental groupoid of commutative rings and Mathew's weak Galois groupoid.
paper.title: Representability of Galois extensions

paper.abstract: We study the Dedekind-MacNeille completion through representable functors on the wide subcategory $\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}$ of posets and lower cut-continuous (closed) maps. On this category the completion is contravariantly functorial and naturally isomorphic to $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}}(-,[1])^{\mathrm{op}}$, via $A\mapsto\chi_A$ and its inverse $f\mapsto f^{-1}(\{0\})$. The naturality of this identification makes the Yoneda lemma applicable: uniqueness of the representing object and the endomorphism monoid of the completion follow formally. We also show that $\mathbf{CLat}_\vee$ is full in $\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}$, that $\mathbf{CLat}_\wedge$ is equivalent to a full subcategory of $\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}^{\mathrm{op}}$, and that the covariant adjunction refines to a $2$-adjunction whose idempotent monad has Eilenberg--Moore algebras equivalent to $\mathbf{CLat}_\vee$.
paper.title: The Dedekind-MacNeille Completion as a Functor

paper.abstract: We introduce a notion of pseudo-morphism for groups, which extends the notion of group morphism from a group to a ring. We show that pseudo-morphisms from a group $G$ to an integral domain $R$ form a filtred Hopf algebra which can be seen as an efficient notion of dual for $G$. We also show that pseudo-morphisms are closely related to the notion of polynomial maps in the sense of Eilenberg-MacLane/Passi, the two notions even coinciding when $G$ is finitely generated and $R$ is a field. It follows that, in that case, polynomial maps are endowed with an Hopf structure. In a second part, we study non repeated Milnor invariants (in the $4$-dimensional context of $2$-string links) from this pseudo-morphism point of view. We show that they form a sub-bialgebra of the Hopf algebra of pseudo-morphisms on the group of $2$-string links up to link-homotopy, and prove that it is isomorphic to an explicit quotient $\textrm{Mil}$ of a polynomial ring. This leads to a fully algebraic description of the group of 2-string links up to link-homotopy as the dual group associated to $\textrm{Mil}$. As a by-product, we obtain that non repeated Milnor invariants are polynomial maps, and we show that this can be used to give a new proof of their finite type property.
paper.title: A notion of pseudo-morphisms with applications to the study of polynomial maps and of link-homotopy groups of 2-string link

paper.abstract: The Extended Persistent Homology Transform (XPHT) describes a shape through the extended persistence diagrams of its directional height functions. We present an algorithm for computing a finite directional sample of the three-dimensional XPHT from a triangulated boundary. Our main construction determines essential first-homology pairings by combining an ordered tree-cotree decomposition with evaluation-dual cocycles. The decomposition supplies a homology basis compatible with the height filtration, while the cocycles are used to determine the essential birth-death pairs. Degree-zero persistence and duality determine the remaining boundary diagrams. Under the boundary-reduction hypotheses and with critical-point sign labels, these diagrams yield the extended persistence of the solid. The resulting procedure uses graph constructions and linear algebra over F2 on boundary meshes extracted from three-dimensional binary images.
paper.title: An Implementation of the 3-Dimensional Extended Persistent Homology Transform

paper.abstract: Let $M$ be a connected oriented closed manifold of dimension $d\geq 2$, equipped with a regular CW structure, and let $P$ be its face poset. We consider the cyclic Hasse diagram $G_P^{\mathrm{cyc}}$, obtained from the directed Hasse diagram $G_P$ by adding an arrow from each maximal cell to every $0$-cell of $M$. Over an arbitrary field $\mathbb K$, we completely describe the path cohomology algebra $PH^*(G_P^{\mathrm{cyc}})$ in terms of the $\mathbb K$-Betti numbers of $M$. In particular, this algebra is not graded commutative whenever the dimension of $H^*(M)$ over $\mathbb K$ is at least 4. This disproves Grigor'yan's conjecture on graded commutativity. Moreover, as $M$ ranges over connected oriented closed surfaces, the even subalgebras $PH^{\mathrm{even}}(G_P^{\mathrm{cyc}})$, regarded as ungraded associative unital $\mathbb K$-algebras, satisfy no common algebraic identity beyond those satisfied by all associative unital $\mathbb K$-algebras. These results distinguish GLMY path cohomology from classical cohomology, whose cup product is graded commutative and whose even subalgebra is commutative. As an application, we construct a digraph $G$ for which the K\"unneth formula for the categorical product $G\times G$ fails, answering a question of Pinto negatively and disproving another conjecture of Grigor'yan.
paper.title: Cyclic Hasse diagrams of manifolds and noncommutative path cohomology

paper.abstract: In this note, we explain the circle action on the Hochschild homology of categories of sheaves and their admissible subcategories in terms of the six-functor formalism using factorization homology, including (quasi-)coherent sheaves on derived stacks, sheaves on manifolds with prescribed microsupports, and Tamarkin categories with prescribed microsupports. We also explain the Gysin sequence for $C_\ell$ and $S^1$-(co)invariants and the K\"unneth sequence for $S^1$-(co)invariants of the Hochschild homology relative to any complex-oriented symmetric monoidal category.
paper.title: Cyclic homology of Sheaf Categories

paper.abstract:
We prove that the group $H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely generated, where $\mathcal{I}_3$ is the Torelli subgroup of the mapping class group of a closed genus-three surface $\Sigma_3$. A key role in the proof is played by establishing the following property: for each symplectic transvection $t_x\in\mathrm{Sp}_{6}(\mathbb{Z})$, we have
  $$
  \bigl(t^{120}_x-1\bigr)^{57}\bigl(t_x^{24}-1\bigr)(t_x-1)^6H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})=0.
  $$
  The proof is based on the study of the spectral sequences associated with the action of $\mathcal{I}_3$ on the Bestvina-Bux-Margalit complex of minimizing cycles and with the actions on certain auxiliary complexes of the stabilizers of two- and three-component multicurves on $\Sigma_3$. The remaining ingredients are Tavgen's theorem, which asserts that $\mathrm{Sp}_{6}(\mathbb{Z})$ has bounded elementary generation, and the result of Kassabov and Putman, which asserts that $H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely generated as a $\mathbb{Z}[\mathrm{Sp}_6(\mathbb{Z})]$-module.
paper.title: Finite generation of the second homology group of the genus three Torelli group

paper.abstract: We classify pointed self-maps of $M=\mathbb{RP}^{3}\#\mathbb{RP}^{3}$ up to pointed homotopy. Using the universal cover $S^2\times\mathbb R$, we reduce the problem to paths in the sphere mapping space with even or odd endpoint conditions. The evaluation fibration, Whitehead products, and a double-coset calculation determine the resulting secondary invariants. The classes inducing the trivial fundamental-group endomorphism split into four families, each in bijection with $\mathbb Z$ after choosing a reference homotopy class. Every other realizable endomorphism sends both standard generators to reflections. For each such endomorphism, the realizable multipliers on $\pi_2(M)\cong\mathbb{Z}$ are precisely the odd integers $d$, and the classes with fixed multiplier are in bijection with $\mathbb Z/|d|\mathbb Z$ after choosing a reference homotopy class. We compute an explicit composition law on the double-reflection submonoid and determine the pointed self-homotopy equivalences. The classes inducing the trivial fundamental-group endomorphism form a subset $\mathcal{T}$ that is preserved by composition on either side with arbitrary pointed homotopy classes and satisfies $\mathcal{T}^2=\{0\}$, where $0$ is the constant class. For each fixed triple $(m,k,d)$ in the double-reflection case, the $|d|$ classes induce identical homomorphisms on every homotopy group. Thus the secondary invariant detects distinctions invisible to these induced homomorphisms.
paper.title: Homotopy Classification of Pointed Self-Maps of $\mathbb{RP}^3\#\mathbb{RP}^3$

paper.abstract: We provide a self-contained exposition of cohesive $(2,1)$-topos theory, its internal synthetic geometry, and its realization of intrinsic, modal, and differential nonabelian cohomology. Starting from the $(2,1)$-categorical hierarchy, Grothendieck $(2,1)$-topoi, effective internal groupoids, and $\E_k$-algebra objects over $(2,1)$-operads, we develop a detailed comparison between \emph{internal} and \emph{external} deloopings in $(2,1)$-presheaf and Grothendieck $(2,1)$-topoi. Specifically, we formalize external delooping by transporting the canonical delooping transformation along the group, discrete, and groupoid Yoneda 2-embeddings, proving that it is 2-naturally equivalent to the internal delooping in any Grothendieck $(2,1)$-topos. We then establish the 2-truncated Dunn--Lurie additivity, Baez--Dolan stabilization, and Eckmann--Hilton characterization of $k$-tuply groupal objects as groupal $\E_k$-algebras stabilizing at $k=3$, and clarify the truncation behavior of iterated deloopings $B_{\mathbf{H}}^k G$. Finally, we review Lawvere--Schreiber cohesive modalities, construct abstract principal $k$-bundles, the flat de Rham modality $\flat_{\dR}$, universal Maurer--Cartan forms $\theta_k$, connection moduli stacks $B^k_{\con}G$, and sharp-adjusted internal connection moduli $G\Conn^k(X)$. The paper culminates in synthetic differential cohomology, where we discuss extensions of the Maurer--Cartan morphism to non-groupal coefficients via $\int_{\dR} \dashv \flat_{\dR}$, and internal classifying structures.
paper.title: Cohesive 2-Topoi: Foundational Aspects and Nonabelian Differential Cohomology

paper.abstract: We develop explicit Frobenius and perfection arguments for framed motives over imperfect fields. In positive characteristic, power framing homotopies and local framed transfers make relative Frobenius invertible after inverting the characteristic. Descent through successive Frobenius twists then gives a proof of strict homotopy invariance for homotopy invariant quasi-stable additive framed presheaves and identifies the canonical comparison with the perfect closure as a stable Nisnevich local equivalence of framed motives. We extend the comparison to E-framed motives for every motivic Thom spectrum E. It also yields the cancellation theorem and the cone theorem. For commutative symmetric Thom ring spectra, we identify triangulated categories of effective E-framed motives and effective E-modules and prove perfection invariance of these triangulated categories. All comparisons are made after inverting the exponential characteristic.
paper.title: Frobenius and perfection in framed motives

paper.abstract: We investigate when the braided monoidal $\infty$-categories of sheaf-theoretic line operators of $3$-dimensional topological quantum field theories are invertible in the higher Morita category, so that they determine invertible $4$-dimensional anomaly theories. We consider a zoo of different examples which are inherently derived. First, enhancing Ben-Zvi--Francis--Nadler, we show that a symmetric monoidal category of quasi-coherent sheaves $\mathrm{QC}(X)$ is invertible only if $X$ is a point, and convolution categories on loop stacks are Morita trivial whenever the stack satisfies descent along its diagonal, e.g. for classifying stacks. Secondly, we provide an example showing that, unlike for finite braided tensor categories, non-degeneracy does not imply invertibility in the derived setting: For an odd vector space $V[1]$, the $2$-shifted $\mathcal{D}$-modules $\mathrm{DMod}^2(V[1])$ are $3$-dualizable and non-degenerate but neither factorizable nor cofactorizable. This category is closely related to the line operators of linear Rozansky--Witten theory. Finally, we define an anomaly of a group action on an invertible braided monoidal $\infty$-category as a Witt class over $\mathrm{Rep}(G)$, and show that the category of representations of the quantum group of a torus at a root of unity is invertible relative to its quantum Frobenius.
paper.title: Towards invertibility of derived categories of sheaf-theoretic line operators

paper.abstract: We study freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks. We show that the associated quandle functor and the associated crossed module functor are left adjoint to the natural forgetful functors. For a map $f\colon S\to G$, we define the free augmented rack $R_f\to G$ and the free augmented quandle $Q_f\to G$. If $C_f\to G$ denotes the free crossed module determined by $f$, then the associated crossed modules of $R_f$ and $Q_f$ are both isomorphic to $C_f\to G$. We also characterize free augmented quandles in terms of stabilizers. As applications, we prove that the canonical inner augmentation of every generalized Alexander quandle is free and that the canonical inner augmentation of a classical knot quandle is free if and only if the knot is a torus knot, whereas for every $n$-knot with $n\geq2$ it is free.
paper.title: Freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks

paper.abstract: The perfect matching complex of a simple graph $G$ is an abstract simplicial complex whose facets (maximal faces) are precisely the perfect matchings of $G$. In this article, we study the topology of the perfect matching complex of the $3\times 2n$ grid graph and show that it is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of $f_{n-1}$ copies of $(n-1)$-dimensional spheres, where $f_{k}$ denotes the $k$-th Fibonacci number. This proves a particular case of the conjecture given by Chandrakar and Singh for perfect matching complex of grid graphs.
paper.title: Perfect Matching Complexes of $3\times 2n$ Grid Graph

paper.abstract:
We establish stability results for internal homs of $\varepsilon$-simplicial sets, a framework motivated by nerves of Frobenius monoids in the category of relations. Rotations are modelled through edge witnesses and horn-filling conditions, without requiring unique fillers. For $\varepsilon$-fibrant objects $X$ and $Y$, we prove that the internal hom $\mathrm{Fun}(X,Y)$ satisfies the $\varepsilon$-coherence conditions and admits fillers for all $\varepsilon$-horns of dimension at least two. Its subobject consisting of simplices whose vertices correspond to $\eta$-edge-preserving maps is $\varepsilon$-fibrant. We also introduce $\eta\varepsilon$-simplicial sets by adding explicit $\eta$-witnesses and prove that the internal hom of two $\eta\varepsilon$-fibrant objects is again $\eta\varepsilon$-fibrant.
  Our proofs use adjunctions relating $\varepsilon$-simplicial sets and paracyclic sets. We characterise the $\varepsilon$-horn filling property by requiring the corresponding counit to be a trivial Kan fibration. Consequently, for every object satisfying this property, coherent choices of rotations of each simplex form a contractible Kan complex.
paper.title: Stability theorems for $\varepsilon$-simplicial sets

paper.abstract: We calculate the mod $2$-homology of the fixed points of the $C_4$-equivariant Hill--Hopkins--Ravenel theory $BP^{((C_4))}\langle 1\rangle$, as an $\mathcal{A}_*$-comodule algebra. $2$-locally these fixed points are $tmf_0(5)$ by a theorem of Quinn. We deduce that $tmf_0(5)$ is an indecomposable $tmf$-module that is an extension of two $tmf$-modules of the form $tmf\otimes K$ for a finite spectrum $K$. The $K(2)$-localization of $tmf_0(5)$ is $32$-periodic, and we compute the Adams spectral sequence of $tmf_0(5)$ through the $32$-stem.
paper.title: On the Adams spectral sequence of $eo_2(C_4)$

paper.abstract: We construct $n$-categories $\mathscr{P}_n$ with generators given by simplices and relations given by bistellar moves between them, in any dimension $n$. We show that functors out of $\mathscr{P}_n$ into an $n$-category of theories, give the correct input for the orbifold construction for TQFTs, and subsume all previously known examples, which are all in dimensions $n \leq 3$. In particular, in dimension 3 the construction gives a highly nontrivial categorification of a kind of nonunital, noncounital, Frobenius algebra.
paper.title: Higher Categorical Bistellar Moves

paper.abstract: In this paper, we study the monoidal category of finite-dimensional right comodules over the path algebra $\Bbbk Q$ of a finite acyclic quiver $Q$, equipped with the weak bialgebra structure in which every path is grouplike. We prove that the lax center of this category is monoidally equivalent to $\operatorname{Rep}^{\mathrm{fd}}_{\Bbbk}(Q)$, the category of finite-dimensional representations of $Q$. We also classify all $\Bbbk$-linear strong monoidal functors between any two such comodule categories, and all monoidal natural transformations between them. For the right adjoint of such a functor, we determine when the left or right projection formula holds. When both projection formulas hold, this adjoint will induce a functor between the lax centers, and we describe the induced functor explicitly on quiver representations.
paper.title: Lax Centers and Monoidal Functors for Comodule Categories Associated with Acyclic Quivers

paper.abstract: We show that all higher Verlinde categories are maximally nilpotent, as conjectured by Coulembier (2023). By previous results, it suffices to show that non-trivial simple objects have only finitely many non-zero symmetric powers in odd characteristic. We compute the maximal degrees of these non-zero symmetric and exterior powers explicitly, hence confirming their finiteness. We discuss some of the far-reaching consequences.
paper.title: Maximal nilpotence for higher Verlinde categories

paper.abstract: Let $a$ denote the stabilization of the Euler class of the sign representation of $\mathrm{C}_2$. In this paper, we show that the Behrens-Shah periodic $u$-self-equivalence of $C(a^i)$ -- a direct consequence of J.F. Adams' calculation of James periodicity -- determines the $\mathrm{H}\underline{\mathbb{F}}_2$-Hurewicz image of the $\mathrm{C}_2$-equivariant sphere spectrum, recovering a recent theorem of Guo-Li-Lu-Wu-Xu-Yang-Zhang via a different method. Furthermore, we use the $\mathrm{C}_2$-equivariant periodic $u$-self-equivalences on the cofiber spectra $C(a^i)$ to construct new infinite families in the $\mathrm{C}_2$-equivariant stable stems whose $\mathrm{H}\underline{\mathbb{F}}_2$-Hurewicz image is trivial.
paper.title: New $\mathrm{C}_2$-equivariant infinite families and the $\mathrm{H}\underline{\mathbb{F}}_2$-Hurewicz image

paper.abstract: We apply a derived completion construction for commutative ring spectra to give a description of the K-theory spectrum of a geometric field F (i.e. containing an algebraically closed subfield $k$) of characteristic zero purely in terms of the representation theory of its absolute Galois group $G_F$. A result that follows is that the l-adically completed Milnor K-theory of F is isomorphic to the derived completion of the representation ring of $G_F$. The main result, from which this follows, is that $K(F)$ completed at l is equivalent to the derived completion of the K-theory of the category of finite dimensional representations of $G_F$ in $k$.
paper.title: Representation Theory and the Algebraic K-Theory of Geometric Fields

paper.abstract: XXX spin-chain Hamiltonians can be derived within the $R$-matrix formalism. For a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$, the rational $R$-matrix $R$ intertwines the coproduct $\Delta$ in the Yangian $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{g})$. $R$ admits a particular Gauss decomposition $R=LDU$, where the upper-triangular matrix $U$ can be obtained from the lower-triangular matrix $L$. We treat $U$ in three ways. Algebraically, $U$ is known as a factorization twist. It plays the role of a ``universalizer'': it conjugates a non-universal pseudo-coproduct $\mathscr{D}$ in the molten crystal chain basis to the true Yangian coproduct $\Delta=U^{-1}\mathscr{D} U$. Physically, $U$ can be obtained as a Berry phase in SUSY quiver QFT for a quiver associated with the Dynkin diagram of $\mathfrak{g}$. In this case, $U$ is calculated as a sum over tunneling amplitudes. Geometrically, $U$ can be interpreted as a renormalized Maulik-Okounkov stable envelope localized at a fixed point. In the physical setting, the Yang-Baxter equation (YBE), which ensures integrability, follows from the flatness of the Berry connection, which in turn follows from supersymmetry. However, the YBE imposes subtle constraints on the tunneling amplitudes, which we examine here. We construct recursion relations that allow higher collective amplitudes to be obtained from more elementary ones. We observe that different tunneling channels are in fact intertwined, leading to finer cancellations among amplitudes and to wall-crossing phenomena: depending on the parameters, the same amplitude is represented as a sum over different channels. We focus on $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ with higher-spin and non-evaluation representations, as well as on the fundamental representation of $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1})$.
paper.title: On Tunnel Fusion and Yangian $R$-matrices

paper.abstract: We compute the asymptotic dimension of spaces of multiparameter persistence modules of bounded presentation under the interleaving distance. The $d$-parameter modules with at most $n$ generators and $m$ relations have asymptotic dimension, and Assouad-Nagata dimension, exactly $d(n+m)$, the number of coordinates of their generator and relation grades, over every field; for two parameters this is $2(n+m)$. The space has continuous moduli, already for two parameters and $n,m\ge2$: over an infinite field it contains, at every scale, infinite uniformly separated families of pairwise non-isomorphic modules with one fibered barcode, so it is not doubling even at a fixed fibered barcode; already for $m\ge1$ it is not coarsely equivalent to a proper metric space. The proof is an induction on the number of distinct grade coordinates: an interleaving small compared with the gaps between these coordinates moves each of them by at most twice its size and preserves the induced grid representation, so the continuous moduli are invisible at large scale. Each class of modules at finite distance therefore embeds coarsely into Hilbert space; for $n,m\ge2$ over an uncountable field, the classes that contain these families admit no such embedding into a separable Hilbert space. Under the two-parameter matching distance $2(n+m)$ is a lower bound, attained for one generator and for two generators with at most one relation; on a finite net of $S$ slices the asymptotic dimension is at most $2nS$.
paper.title: Asymptotic Dimension of Persistence Modules of Bounded Presentation

paper.abstract: We study Chern characteristic classes of normal vector bundles of complex generalized flag submanifolds $G_{n-1}/P_{n-1}$ in complex generalized flag manifolds $G_n/P_n$. This procedure can be regarded as the relative version of Schubert calculus for the pair $G_{n-1}/P_{n-1}$ and $G_n/P_n$. The CW structure and additive structure of the cohomology of $\mathrm{Gr}(n, k)$ allows inductive calculation of Chern classes of the canonical and complementary canonical vector bundles over $\mathrm{Gr}(n, k)$. The combination of representation theory and algebraic geometry allows to derive analogous properties for the isotropic Grassmannians $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$ via their embeddings in $\mathrm{Gr}(m, k)$. Then the induced CW structure yields the additive structure on the cohomology of $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$, and consequently leads to the calculation of Chern classes of the canonical and complementary canonical vector bundles over $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$.
paper.title: Chern characteristic classes of normal bundles of complex generalized flag submanifolds in generalized flag manifolds

paper.abstract: Geometric chains are formal combinations of smooth maps from compact oriented manifolds or orbifolds with corners. In earlier work the author showed that, modulo a relation D that kills degenerate chains, they compute rational singular homology. We show that D can be replaced by a gluing relation, which identifies a chain with the sum of its restrictions to finitely many pieces whenever its source is glued from these pieces along whole codimension-one faces. With this relation the comparison map from singular homology is an isomorphism in all degrees for compact polyhedra and smooth manifolds without boundary, with rational and with integer coefficients. Unlike D, the gluing relation is defined through the sources alone, and chain-level identities such as the equivalence of a degree d covering with d times its base, which fails modulo D, and the correction terms of the chain map from a Morse complex, which are degenerate modulo D, become gluing relations. The proof is axiomatic; injectivity comes from integration or dual cells, surjectivity from cutting along regular levels, where the cut of a gluing relation is again one, and at the point we use Whitehead triangulations of manifolds with corners subordinate to their corner strata. The gluing relation, read on underlying spaces, also suffices for orbifold sources, with integer coefficients modulo classes with an orientation reversing automorphism, and for effective orbifold targets.
paper.title: Gluing Geometric Chains Of Manifolds And Orbifolds With Corners

paper.abstract: We consider a version of Legendrian contact homology filtered by the action of Reeb chords. In this version, a union of two disjoint exact Lagrangian cobordisms with Legendrian boundary conditions gives rise to a morphism between persistence modules. We discuss a certain algebraic invariant of such morphisms and use it to obtain obstructions to Lagrangian isotopies of the cobordisms, as well as applications to symplectic and contact dynamics.
paper.title: Lagrangian cobordisms and morphisms of persistence modules

paper.abstract: The path homology theory is based on the notion of path complex and is a part of GLMY-theory created and developed by Grigor'yan, Lin, Muranov, and Yau in a cycle of papers in 2012-2014. In this paper we define a path complex with concatenation ($PC$-complex) which is a particular case of a path complex. We define a natural topology on a set of vertices of any $PC$-complex, and describe properties of this topology and its relation to the discrete topology of Alexandroff. We prove the existence of functorial relations between some categories of $PC$-complexes and digraphs. These relations allow to transfer covering, homotopy and various versions of homology theory from digraph theory to $PC$-complexes.
paper.title: Path complexes with concatenation and their relation to digraphs

paper.abstract: We give explicit and recursive formulas for the Poincar\'e polynomials of Dani--Mainkar nilmanifolds associated with path graphs. We also prove that these polynomials are unimodal, and we calculate a range of Betti numbers asymptotically. As an application, we derive a sharp lower bound for the dimension of the total de Rham cohomology of a Dani--Mainkar nilmanifold.
paper.title: Poincar\'e polynomials of nilmanifolds associated with path graphs

paper.abstract: We describe a quantization procedure for Betti mapping stacks with shifted Poisson targets by combining factorization homology and formal geometry. We quantize derived stacks of local systems of low-dimensional manifolds.
paper.title: Quantization of Betti Mapping Stacks

paper.abstract: Given a locally finite open cover of a paracompact space, a subordinate partition of unity defines a map into the geometric realization of the nerve. When the cover is good, the nerve theorem asserts that this map is a homotopy equivalence. In applied topology, one specializes this construction to covers of metric data by open balls centered at finitely many landmarks. The corresponding nerve map represents the data inside the \v{C}ech complex, enabling one to pull cohomological or spectral invariants back to the data. Since point cloud data often comes equipped with weights encoding domain-specific importance, we introduce a weighted version of the nerve map and study its stability under perturbations of the landmarks and weights using metrics from optimal transport. Our main result is a Lipschitz stability theorem for the weighted nerve map under a uniform nondegeneracy assumption. We state the bound in terms of a scale-dependent optimal transport distance, and give an example where our estimate is attained. Since this distance is dominated by a multiple of the $1$-Wasserstein distance, Wasserstein stability follows as a corollary. We also give geometric conditions ensuring nondegeneracy, obtain explicit estimates of the Lipschitz constant for closed Riemannian manifolds, and sketch applications to Laplacian eigenvector cascading and Eilenberg--MacLane coordinates.
paper.title: Wasserstein Stability of the Nerve Map

paper.abstract: We study the restriction data carried by dependent-product extension along a monomorphism. In a locally cartesian closed category, the extended map is an isomorphism after a change of base if and only if the input map is an isomorphism on the restricted base. In a topos, its isomorphism locus is therefore the universal quantification of the input locus. A terminal characterization gives coherent comparisons for base change and successive extension, together with formulas for intersections and unions. Under explicit homotopical, cartesian, and universe hypotheses, this construction gives equivalence extension and preserves the boundary identifications used to prove fibrancy of a universe. Graph comparisons and strict fillers of a fixed universe boundary are represented by trivially fibrant objects. A single realignment over the comparison object induces a weak equivalence between these parameter objects, and both admit extensions of every finite cubical boundary. A finite-groupoid example shows that graph comparisons cannot be selected naturally under all isomorphisms of unstructured input.
paper.title: Isomorphism Loci and Coherence in Equivalence Extension

paper.abstract: Finster, Kleiner, and Paganini derived from causal fermion systems (CFS) a nonrelativistic effective collapse model whose statistical operator obeys, to leading order, a Kossakowski--Lindblad equation. In the factorized regime of that derivation, the dissipator is built from purely spatial operators $N_{k,a}$ with positive rates fixed by microscopic time-nonlocal kernels. We translate this CFS-specific generator into quantities accessible to coherent quantum processors. The resulting CFS Dirichlet form obeys an exact purity-loss identity under arbitrary Hamiltonian control, and its null algebra is the commutant of the $*$-algebra generated by the projected $N_{k,a}$. For joint eigenbranches we obtain an exact distinguishability functional controlling exponential coherence loss and a lower bound on channel distance from ideal unitary evolution. In an $n$-qubit dephasing sector, the projected kernels generate a positive-semidefinite covariance matrix $C$, with GHZ visibility $\exp[-2T\bm{1}^{\mathsf T}C\bm{1}]$. We prove that uniformly summable finite-range correlations yield at most $O(n)$ GHZ decay, whereas $O(n^2)$ scaling requires a collective non-summable component. Single- and two-qubit cat coherences reconstruct $C$, giving a covariance-spectroscopy protocol, while Knill--Laflamme conditions characterize first-order correctability of the projected CFS error algebra. We also derive an explicit compatibility inequality between macroscopic state reduction and long coherent computation and show why absence of probe heating does not imply absence of coherence signatures. The results do not exclude CFS: its covariance strength, $\ellmin$, and hardware projection remain underdetermined. They instead identify the microscopic input required for a genuine no-go theorem and establish scalable quantum processors as direct probes of the CFS collapse sector.
paper.title: Quantum-Information Probes of Collapse Dynamics in Causal Fermion Systems

paper.abstract: In the absence of a theory of closed immersions in tensor-triangular geometry, we propose an alternative approach via quotients of module categories. As an application, we prove invariance of homological residue fields under completion.
paper.title: Closed layers in tensor-triangular geometry

paper.abstract:
In analogy with the passage from connective to non-connective algebraic K-theory, Schlichting put forward the Karoubi-Grothendieck-Witt spectrum as an approximation to Grothendieck-Witt theory by a functor invariant under idempotent completion. In this paper, we extend his construction to the setting of Poincar\'e $\infty$-categories and characterise the resulting functor by the expected universal property.
  Our main result places these Karoubi-Grothendieck-Witt-spectra in an exact sequence involving the ultimately decorated L-spectrum and homotopy orbits of non-connective K-theory. This confirms a conjecture of Williams which had remained open even for rings in which $2$ is invertible, and allows us to deduce universal characterisations for ultimately decorated L-theory. We obtain these results by unifying the Bass-Heller-Swan and Ranicki-Shaneson splittings into a general decomposition theorem that yields, in particular, formulas for Grothendieck-Witt groups of Laurent polynomial rings.
  Finally, we construct multiplicative structures on both versions of our Grothendieck-Witt and L-functors and refine their universal properties to multiplicative ones. Along the way, we show that the original versions are even idempotent with respect to Day convolution.
paper.title: Hermitian K-theory for stable $\infty$-categories IV: Karoubi-Grothendieck-Witt theory

paper.abstract: In the first half of these notes, we survey some aspects of the stack-theoretic perspective on $p$-adic Hodge theory, with an emphasis on the non-abelian aspects. In the second half, we report ongoing joint work on ``quantizing'' non-abelian $p$-adic Hodge theory.
paper.title: Non-abelian $p$-adic Hodge theory and stacks

paper.abstract: We prove an equivariant coarse Green--Julg theorem for proper isometric actions of countable discrete groups on bounded geometry metric spaces. We introduce the $(\Gamma, X)$-controlled proper $C^{*}$-algebra, and show that the evaluation-at-zero map between the equivariant localization and Roe algebras with such coefficients induces an isomorphism on $K$-theory.
paper.title: An Equivariant Coarse Green-Julg Theorem for Proper Actions

paper.abstract: Let $n\geq0$ and let $\mathcal X$ be a bounded coherent $\infty$-topos. Suppose that finitely many noninitial coherent $n$-truncated objects cover its terminal object, and that every coherent $n$-truncated object in each of their slices has a finite covering family of sections. We identify $\mathcal X^{\mathrm{coh}}_{\leq n}$ with $\operatorname{Fun}(M,\mathcal S_{\pi,\leq n})$ for a $\pi$-finite $(n+1)$-type $M$, recovered by all finite models preserving finite limits, finite coproducts, and effective epimorphisms. Descent uses degrees through $n+2$ for objects and $n+1$ for maps; both bounds are sharp for finite homotopy actions. Every exact functor $F$ between recognized categories has a universal parameter $P_F=F_!(1)$ and a canonical factorization through its slice with fully faithful second functor. This parameter characterizes full faithfulness, conservativity, and all exact slice factorizations. For successive abelian Postnikov layers, we identify the space of marked exact lifts with a path space of Eilenberg--Mac Lane sections with local coefficients. The obstruction, classes of lifts, and relative automorphisms occur in degrees $r+1$, $r$, and $r-1$. We compute a twisted parity obstruction and, for odd primes, classify cyclic self-equivalence components by a $p$-adic valuation. A nonzero Postnikov class can persist in the identity component. For continuous finite families over a profinite $(n+1)$-type, we prove that a uniform finite-section atlas exists precisely when the complete model space is $\pi$-finite. Exact functors from finite model semantics, together with their lift spaces, satisfy finite-stage descent, while explicit profinite examples separate objectwise trivialization from uniform parameter elimination.
paper.title: Higher Galois Recognition and Parameter Descent

paper.abstract: We develop a viewpoint of Pin(2)-equivariant Bauer-Furuta invariant: It can be converted to a section over a finite dimensional Pin(2)-orbit, and it takes values in ordinary stable homotopy class. This viewpoint reveals a topological limitation of the invariant: If the fiber's connectivity exceeds the dimension of the base space, then all sections are homotopic to the trivial section. We use it to recover Lin-Mukherjee vanishing theorem. Furthermore, the family Seiberg-Witten invariant can be obtained from the pullback of such sections to $S^1$-orbit. We use this fact to prove a vanishing theorem of the Pin(2)-equivariant family Bauer-Furuta invariant after two stabilizations.
paper.title: Vanishing Theorem of Pin(2)-equivariant Bauer-Furuta Invariants as Stable Sections

paper.abstract: It is a folk theorem of Goodwillie that there are exactly 9 model structures on the category of sets, coming from 18 pre-model structures. We investigate model structures and pre-model structures on the category of $G$-sets for a finite group $G$. We outline a strategy for finding all model structures in this category, and partially execute this strategy for the case of $C_p$-sets, where $C_p$ denotes a cyclic group of prime order $p$. In particular, there are exactly 1777 pre-model structures on the category of $C_p$-sets.
paper.title: Pre-Model Structures on the Category of $C_p$-Sets

paper.abstract: Let $X_1,\dots,X_N$ be independent uniform points in the unit square, matched either to an evenly spread deterministic configuration or to a second independent sample. For exponents $\alpha_1,\alpha_2>2$ with $1/\alpha_1+1/\alpha_2=1/2$, we prove that with probability tending to one a single permutation controls the $j$th coordinate displacements in the exponential Orlicz norm of exponent $\alpha_j$, at the scale $\sqrt{\log N/N}$, for both $j=1,2$. This settles Talagrand's Ultimate Matching Conjecture for all pairs of finite critical exponents. The proof constructs, on the flat torus, a current whose divergence is Gaussian white noise projected on a dyadic grid and whose coordinates have the critical anisotropic exponential Orlicz bounds, and transfers it to matching through a primal optimal-transport reduction. At the hard endpoints $(2,\infty)$ and $(\infty,2)$ the conjecture fails: a Brownian local-time construction shows that the normalized optimal matching cost diverges in probability.
paper.title: The Ultimate Matching Theorem

paper.abstract: We study the number of non-cyclic Sylow subgroups of $(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)^\times$. Pollack suggested investigating whether this count has a limiting distribution after suitable normalization. For uniformly chosen $n\le x$, we prove a Gaussian limit with variance asymptotic to $\tfrac12\log_2x/\log_3x$. Motivated by the fixed-rank normal-order results of Morales, Polanco, and Pollack, we further prove joint Gaussian limits for this count and the numbers of elementary abelian Sylow subgroups of any fixed finite collection of ranks at least two. We give explicit prime-sum centers and asymptotics for all arithmetic covariances. The same joint theorem includes the number of common prime divisors of Euler's and Dedekind's functions. The proof uses the integer Kubilius model, estimates for the dependence between distinct output primes, and mean-square bounds for arithmetic truncation.
paper.title: Gaussian limits for non-cyclic and elementary abelian Sylow subgroups of the multiplicative group

paper.abstract: We give the first complete topological, geometric, and ergodic classification of the Ziegler spectrum $\Zg(\Lambda)$ of a non-domestic string algebra $\Lambda$ over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary cardinality, via a dictionary with Thurston's theory of geodesic laminations on a cusped hyperbolic surface. This is a model-theoretic counterpart of Haiden--Katzarkov--Kontsevich's realization (\emph{Publ.\ Math.\ IHES} 2017) of stability conditions on the bounded derived category of a gentle algebra via flat surfaces: pure-injective modules correspond to admissible geodesics, and the Ziegler topology to a corridor quotient of Chabauty space. Three consequences follow. The Krull--Gabriel dimension equals the surface's topological accumulation depth, and the string closure with all higher Cantor--Bendixson strata is globally homeomorphic to an explicit corridor space, with the pushout map to $\Zg(\Lambda)$ a homeomorphism if and only if $\Lambda$ is domestic. Prefix-free dyadic blocks in the geometric perfect core verify Puninski's cardinality-free two-chain criterion, resolving the open problem of superdecomposable pure-injectives over uncountable fields for all non-domestic string and special biserial algebras. Three purely algebraic invariants on the perfect core---localized pp-shape entropy, a $K_0$-weighted pressure function satisfying an algebraic Ruelle--Walters Variational Principle, and a pp-bifurcation index with a Gauss--Bonnet simplicity obstruction---strictly separate uncountable iso-entropic and iso-pressure families, and the inverse limit of the quotient pp-lattice recovers the transversal Cantor cross-section.
paper.title: Geometric Hammocks: Surface Laminations and the Ziegler Spectrum of String Algebras

paper.abstract: In this paper, we study the orbit manifolds of free diagonal linear circle actions on \(S^{2n+1}\times S^{2n+1}\). For every \(n\geq 1\), we establish a PL homeomorphism classification of the orbit manifolds in terms of the weights of the actions. We also obtain diffeomorphism classification and homotopy classification of such orbit manifolds in dimension $9$ and $13$. The diffeomorphism classification results lead to two geometric applications. For every \(m\geq 1\), there exist a non-spin \(9\)-manifold \(M_m^9\) and a spin \(13\)-manifold \(M_m^{13}\) in our family such that the moduli space of unit-volume homogeneous Einstein metrics on each manifold has at least \(2^{m-1}\) connected components. Moreover, each of these manifolds admits at least \(2^{m-1}\) regular Sasakian structures whose underlying contact structures are pairwise non-contactomorphic.
paper.title: Linear circle quotients of products of odd-dimensional spheres: classification and geometric applications

paper.abstract: For sections between simply connected spaces of finite rational type, we compare module sectional category, sectional category and relative category after rationalization. Fibre Poincar\'e duality turns the compatibility of derived evaluation with the section into a derived self-intersection formula. We prove equality of the three invariants under any of four hypotheses: a base-dimension bound, finite total rational homotopy of the fibre, a smooth section with closed manifold fibre, or a compatible relative Frobenius model. Projective bundles over CP^k with fibre CP^r have common value k + r, which is unbounded even for fixed fibre. Whether fibre Poincar\'e duality alone suffices remains open.
paper.title: Thom Morphisms, Self-Intersection, and the Sectional Category of a Section

paper.abstract: We establish a criterion for determining when a family of geometric functors is jointly conservative through the lens of purity in compactly generated triangulated categories. We introduce the notion of pure descendability and we apply it to two particular situations involving sequential limits of ring spectra.
paper.title: Conservative geometric functors via purity

paper.abstract: We formulate discrete dynamics internally in the topos Cond of condensed sets. For an endomorphism $f\colon X\to X$, we construct orbit quotients, backward histories, preimage trees, and periodic loci as objects evaluated on profinite parameter spaces. The framework recovers global-section dynamics, fully faithfully embeds compact Hausdorff systems, characterizes the invertible extension, and is compatible with inverse limits. It organizes $p$-adic congruence towers and shows, for a Cantor-type non-Archimedean Julia set, that classical periodic points can be dense although the internal periodic locus is not isomorphic to the compact condensed Julia set.
paper.title: An introduction to discrete dynamics in condensed sets: orbits, periodic loci, and arithmetic examples

paper.abstract: We introduce a concept of counital comodule algebra $(B,\delta_B,\epsilon_B)$ over a Hopf ${\mathbb K}$-algebra $H$, where $\delta_B: B\rightarrow B \otimes H$ and $\epsilon_B: B\rightarrow {\mathbb K}$ are coaction and counit homomorphisms, respectively. This structure gives a canonical (counital) comodule algebra map $\iota_B: B \rightarrow H$. In this paper, we study in details the case $B=O_q$, and $H$ is the quantum loop algebra ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$ for ${\mathbb K}={\mathbb C}$. Here, $O_q$ is the $q$-Onsager algebra with four presentations: (i) the $q$-Dolan-Grady type; (ii) the alternating type; (iii) the root vectors type; (iv) the Drinfeld type. For $(O_q,\delta_{O_q},\epsilon_{O_q})$, in fact a 3-parameter family of counital comodule algebras, we establish a Faddeev-Reshetikhin-Takhtajan (FRT) type presentation, which is written in terms of a K-operator satisfying a reflection algebra relation. The coaction $\delta_{O_q}$ (resp. $\iota_{O_q}$) sends the K-operator to a `dressed' K-operator (resp. K-matrix) using Ding-Frenkel type L-operators of ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$; the counit $\epsilon_{O_q}$ sends the K-operator to the most general (non-diagonal) solution of the reflection equation. The FRT presentation allows to compute the image via $\delta_{O_q}$ and $\iota_{O_q}$ of the generating functions of $O_q$ for each presentation (ii)-(iv). Moreover, the images of Lu-Wang's generating functions of $O_q$ in the so-called Drinfeld second realization ${}^{Dr}\!{\cal L}U_qsl_2$ are obtained, as well as their images via the (ordinary) coproduct of ${}^{Dr}\!{\cal L}U_qsl_2$, which enhance two theorems by Prze\'zdziecki. Finally, we apply our FRT presentation to the construction of new type $q$-characters for ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$, in imaginary root vectors of $O_q$, refining those of Frenkel-Reshetikhin, and we explain representation-theoretic meaning of such refining.
paper.title: FRT presentation of the $q$-Onsager comodule algebra and refined $q$-characters

paper.abstract: Working in homotopy type theory, we define relative homotopy groups and give three equivalent definitions of the product on these groups. Using this product, we establish the multiplicativity of the cohomological Serre spectral sequence. We show a connection between the homotopy product and the cup-product in cohomology, which leads to the classically familiar description of the starting page of the spectral sequence as a tensor product of graded rings. As applications, we compute cohomology rings of several classifying spaces and loop spaces of spheres.
paper.title: Multiplicativity of the Serre Spectral Sequence in Homotopy Type Theory

paper.abstract: We make two case studies of $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded homotopy in connection with $p$-adic cohomology. First, we identify the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf T)$-graded $\mathrm{TC}^-$ and $\mathrm{TP}$ of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings as multi-Rees algebras for the Nygaard and $\phi^\bullet(I)$-adic filtrations. We additionally compute $E^{h\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ and $E^{t\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ when $E$ is a general even $\mathbf E_\infty$-ring with $\mathbf T$-action, and compute $(\mathrm{TR}^n)^{h\mathbf T/C_{p^n}}_\bigstar$ in terms of iterated Nygaard filtrations. Next, we compute the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf Z_p)^\land$-graded $\mathrm{TR}$ of smooth algebras over a perfectoid base, providing a pushout of the works of Hesselholt and Angeltveit-Gerhardt along the base case $\mathbf F_p$. Using this, we extend Angeltveit's Norm map of Witt vectors to the de Rham-Witt complex, which participates in a "Witt coordinates" decomposition of the $p$-primary Adams operations.
paper.title: $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded norms for de Rham-Witt forms

paper.abstract: We prove motivic mirror symmetry for full-rank sink-recurrent cluster varieties. We allow skew-symmetrizable principal parts and invert all frozen variables. The rational geometric motive of such a variety is isomorphic to the additive orbifold motive of the mirror stack of Hu and Shende. This gives comparisons of cohomology, higher Chow groups, and algebraic $K$-theory with rational coefficients. The proof combines quantum deformation with the splitting of these motives into Tate summands. For really full-rank skew-symmetric seeds, a finite \'{e}tale morphism realizes the comparison. We also study this geometric comparison in families over the projective line.
paper.title: Motivic Mirror Symmetry for Sink-recurrent Cluster Varieties

paper.abstract: This expository note gives a short derivation of the classical Spivak normal fibration formula for the total space of a spherical fibration over a Poincar\'e duality space. We review the associated smooth, PL, and topological manifold realization criteria and illustrate them with examples from the stable stems. The principal application combines these criteria with the completed solution of the Kervaire invariant problem to identify the exceptional stems in a specified family of three cell Poincar\'e spaces.
paper.title: On Poincar\'e spaces which are not manifolds

paper.abstract: We study the perfect loop space $LX$ of a proper scheme $X$ over a local field $F$. We show that if $X$ contains a rational curve, then $LX$ is not ind-representable, even in a very weak sense. We also show that if $X$ admits a proper model $\mathfrak{X}$ over the integers $\mathcal{O}$ of $F$, whose geometric special fiber does not contain rational curves, then $L^+\mathfrak{X} \stackrel{\sim}{\to} LX$ is an isomorphism via the natural map, where $L^+\mathfrak{X}$ denotes the perfect positive loop space (jet scheme) of $\mathfrak{X}$. In particular, $LX$ is a scheme in this case.
paper.title: Perfect loops of proper schemes

paper.abstract: We provide a common explanation for two 4-periodic phenomena arising in the study of connective real K-theory: first, the family of twists of ko over $B\mathbb Z/2$, and second, the torsion in the Picard group of $Q_1$-local $\mathcal A(1)$-modules. These phenomena have been previously studied, as they lead to 4-periodic patterns in Smith homomorphisms, resp. in the ko-homology of $(B\mathbb Z/2)^n$. In this paper, we exhibit both of these 4-periodicities as consequences of an isomorphism of two extraspecial groups of order 32.
paper.title: A tale of two periodicities

paper.abstract: We study coarse embeddings into Hilbert space and the asymptotic dimension of spaces of persistence diagrams and multiparameter persistence modules. We replace doubling, the usual hypothesis for landmark embeddings, by admissible tent covers of bounded multiplicity at every scale: stacking them across dyadic scales gives an explicit $1$-Lipschitz coarse embedding, with lower gauge $c\sqrt{\tau t}$, or nearly linear for slowly decaying weights, and the same covers bound the asymptotic dimension by the multiplicity. The spaces of persistence diagrams are not doubling but carry such covers, and for diagrams with $n$ points our covers improve the constant of the known landmark embedding by a factor exponential in $n$. Slice by slice, the construction embeds multiparameter modules with boundedly many bars per slice under the matching distance on any finite net of slices, a class that contains the modules with at most $n$ generators. Bounding bars or persistent Betti numbers instead of generators fails: two-parameter modules with one bar on every slice have infinite asymptotic dimension, and neither they nor the modules of bounded support and bounded rank admit a coarse embedding into Hilbert space, under the matching or the interleaving distance.
paper.title: Coarse Embeddings Beyond Doubling: Persistence Diagrams and Multiparameter Modules

paper.abstract: In this paper, we show that a proper continuous open discrete map from the open unit ball $B^n$ onto a domain in $\R^n$ with $n\geq5$ is a homeomorphism whenever its branch set is compact. This answers Vuorinen's question affirmatively in every dimension $n\ge5.$ In dimension four, we also show that, under the additional assumption of quasiregularity, the map is a quasiconformal homeomorphism. Together with the three-dimensional theorem of Kauranen, Luisto and Tengvall, these results answer the quasiregular question posed as Problem~7.66 in the collections of Barth--Brannan--Hayman and Hayman--Lingham in every dimension $n\ge3$.
paper.title: Compact branch sets and injectivity of proper branched coverings

paper.abstract: For a simple graph $\Gamma$ without loops and an integer $n\geq2$, Abrams showed in his Ph.D. thesis that the discrete configuration space $DConf(\Gamma,n)$ is homeomorphic to a closed $n$-manifold if and only if $n=2$ and $\Gamma$ is $K_5$ or $K_{3,3}$, the two minimal obstructions to graph planarity. We show that this manifold property persists for the infinite family of discrete configuration spaces obtained by replacing the Kuratowski graphs with the $d$-skeleton of the simplex of dimension $2d+2$, thus recovering Abrams' $K_5$ case when $d=1$. Our manifold recognition argument relies on a recursive application of Whitehead's theorem that collapsible PL manifolds are PL balls, combined with Forman's discrete Morse theory. The resulting construction produces an infinite family of combinatorial spheres that contains the Legendre polytope boundaries and is closed under taking vertex links.
paper.title: Discrete Configuration Spaces of Simplex Skeleta: a Middle-Dimensional Manifold Phenomenon

paper.abstract: We present an elementary argument showing that fundamental groups of permutation complexes are free. Hence, $\mathbb{R} P^2$ cannot be realized by a permutation complex, answering a question of Chach\'olski, Levi and Meshulam.
paper.title: Fundamental Groups of Permutation Complexes

paper.abstract: Local anomaly polynomials describe local variations, but a normalized Green-Schwarz phase also depends on global background data. We explain this dependence for ten-dimensional three-sphere bundles of quaternionic lines over closed spin seven-manifolds. The backgrounds retain two specified $\mathrm{Spin}(16)$ gauge bundles and an integral differential trivialization on the base, including its boundary identifications. The trivialized class is the sum of half the first Pontryagin class of the tangent bundle and the second Chern class of the quaternionic line's underlying complex bundle. For these backgrounds, the calculation combines a generally nonzero local Green-Schwarz integral with a real eta invariant evaluated by a twelve-dimensional Atiyah-Patodi-Singer filling. Together, these terms determine an integral relative characteristic number; the additive response is one third of that number, modulo integers. When the base's third and fourth rational cohomology groups vanish, the response equals eight times the Crowley-Goette invariant, without assuming that the base is simply connected. A calibration using the actual quaternionic line bundle gives additive value one third on $\mathrm{Sp}(2)$, recovering the known third-root phase. Distinct integral String data on one fixed ten-manifold give all three phase values, showing which global background information the response can detect. The physical identifications retain their prescribed fermion data, while the separate application to integral topological modular forms and vertex operator superalgebras requires compatible integral lifts. The response calculation constructs neither a microscopic realization nor an equivalence of complete theories.
paper.title: Global Green-Schwarz response on quaternionic sphere bundles

paper.abstract: In this paper, we compute the group of homotopy equivalences of closed, smooth, simply connected $6$-manifolds whose integral homology groups are isomorphic to whose of the complex projective space $\mathbb C \mathrm P^3$, building on computations of their mapping class groups.
paper.title: On the homotopy automorphism group of simply-connected homology $\mathbb C \mathrm P^3$

paper.abstract: We show that the amenable category is monotone with respect to the domination relation for geometric $4$-manifolds and their connected sums.
paper.title: On the monotonicity of amenable category for geometric 4-manifolds and their connected sums

paper.abstract:
We introduce the landscape velocity $\xi$, a scalar measure of variation of a parameter-dependent persistence landscape. For families of finite barcodes whose bars are all born at the fixed filtration value $0$, we show that $\xi$ is the $L^2$ speed of the landscape curve where the sorted death times are differentiable and derive an exact closed formula that requires no persistence landscape at all: the death times of the barcodes, as functions of the parameter, suffice. For the velocity of the empirical mean of several landscapes we also prove a closed formula which, again, strikingly requires neither the empirical mean landscape nor any of the individual landscapes, only the individual barcodes.
  As an application, we revisit Olsthoorn's persistent homology analysis of the transverse-field Ising chain. Whereas his approach uses different homology degrees and summaries depending on the boundary conditions, ours uses $H_0$ only and a single rule: the position of the maximum of $\xi$. This rule locates the quantum critical point for both periodic and open boundary conditions, and for both mutual-information and correlator-based dissimilarities. The position of the maximum converges to the critical point faster than all the estimators we can extract from Olsthoorn's work. In the 4 scenarios considered (different boundary conditions and different dissimilarity matrices), the peak of the normalized velocity becomes increasingly pronounced with system size, with observed logarithmic growth. This logarithmic growth is proved for periodic boundaries with correlator dissimilarity under stated hypotheses, identifying landscape velocity as a singular topological response to quantum criticality.
paper.title: Persistence landscape velocity: Closed formulas and a topological probe of quantum criticality

paper.abstract: We introduce an $\infty$-categorical model of operad pairs and their associated bimonoidal categories. We study the related concepts such as cocartesian-cartesian operad pairs, algebra pairs and the Day convolution. Using the Day convolution for operad pairs, we can define distributive functors between a symmetric bimonoidal category and a cartesian closed monoidal category. As an application, we show that for a finite group $G$, the operadic distributive functors from $\mathrm{Span}(\mathsf{Fin}_G)$ to any cartesian closed monoidal category coincides with the distributive functors defined by the distributive diagram. Therefore, we show that the connective $G$-equivariant $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-ring spectra are equivalently the spectral $G$-Tambara functors.
paper.title: Infinity operad pairs, higher distributivity and spectral Tambara functors

paper.abstract: We prove that the space of equivariant $h$-cobordisms on a smooth $G$-manifold $M$ has a tom Dieck style splitting, after stabilization. As an intermediate step, we introduce a space of isovariant $h$-cobordisms on $M$ and prove that this space also has a splitting, even before stabilizing. This completes the proof of the equivariant version of Waldhausen's stable parametrized $h$-cobordism theorem. Along the way, we establish several foundational results on equivariant smooth manifolds with corners.
paper.title: The splitting of the stable space of equivariant $h$-cobordisms

paper.abstract: We characterise the two-step nilpotent varieties of algebras: the semi-abelian varieties in which all ternary cosmash products vanish. Just as abelian varieties are the categories of modules over a ring, two-step nilpotent varieties are exactly the categories of modules over a square ring in the sense of Baues, Hartl and Pirashvili. We construct the square ring explicitly from the full subcategory on the free algebras on one and two generators, and give complete proofs. As consequences we obtain a description of any two-step nilpotent variety by generators and relations, an intrinsic characterisation in terms of quadratic term operations, and an account of its abelian core and of the lower central series of its objects in terms of the square ring. Along the way, we associate with any commutative ring $R$ a square ring whose modules, the two-step nilpotent $R$-groups, extend Hall's nilpotent $R$-groups of class two from $2$-binomial rings to arbitrary rings of coefficients.
paper.title: Two-step nilpotent varieties as categories of modules over a square ring

paper.abstract: Let $N$ denote the closed non-orientable surface of Euler characteristic $-1$, i.e. the connected sum of three real projective planes $N = \mathbb{RP}^2 \# \mathbb{RP}^2 \# \mathbb{RP}^2$, with fundamental group presented as $\langle A,B,C \mid A^2 B^2 C^2 = I \rangle$ via the standard symmetric cross-cap model. Building on the classical trace-coordinate methods of Fricke, Vogt, and Goldman for free groups, and on the qualitative study of representation varieties of non-orientable surfaces by Benyash-Krivets and Chernousov, we give an explicit affine equation for a dense open piece of the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ GIT character variety $X(N)$. We prove that the trace coordinates $a = \mathrm{tr}(A)$, $b = \mathrm{tr}(B)$, $c = \mathrm{tr}(C)$, $p = \mathrm{tr}(AB)$ satisfy the polynomial relation $c^2 = abp - a^2 - b^2 + 4$, that this hypersurface is smooth and irreducible, and that on the open locus $c \neq 0$ it is isomorphic to the image of $X(N)$ under the trace map, with the remaining trace coordinates $\mathrm{tr}(BC)$, $\mathrm{tr}(CA)$, $\mathrm{tr}(ABC)$ recovered as regular functions on this locus. We further identify the boundary locus $c = 0$ with representations satisfying the matrix identity $A^2 B^2 = -I$, and describe its representation-theoretic structure, while leaving a complete global classification along this locus as an open problem. All key trace identities are proved from Cayley-Hamilton first principles and independently checked numerically against explicit matrices.
paper.title: An Explicit Equation for the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ Character Variety of $\mathbb{RP}^2 \# \mathbb{RP}^2 \# \mathbb{RP}^2$

paper.abstract: In the lower-star filtration (LSF), simplices are assigned filtration values according to the maximum-vertex rule, with each simplex entering the filtration when its highest-valued vertex appears. A limitation of this construction is that some higher-dimensional simplices may enter simultaneously with their boundary faces, causing certain topological features to be filled immediately upon formation and thus not appear in the resulting persistence diagram. To address this limitation, we propose three alternative filtration methods: the \(\varepsilon\)-lower-star filtration (ELSF), the \(L_p\) filtration (LpF), and the softmax filtration (SMF). {ELSF introduces a dimension-dependent delay to the maximum-vertex rule,} allowing higher-dimensional simplices to enter the filtration after their boundary faces, whereas {LpF and SMF use aggregation functions that depend on all vertex values rather} than solely on their maximum. By modifying how filtration values are assigned, these methods allow simplices to enter the filtration more progressively, so that topological features such as loops and voids may persist over longer filtration intervals rather than being filled immediately. Consequently, the resulting persistence diagrams may include persistence features that are not observed under LSF, potentially providing useful information for distinguishing data populations. Experimental results on simulated and real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed filtration methods are computationally efficient and can provide greater sensitivity to structural differences in the data than LSF.
paper.title: Beyond the Lower-Star Filtration: Alternative Filtration Methods for Persistent Homology

paper.abstract: We prove that for any regular CW-complex $X$ there exists a quotient map $X\to Y$ that is a weak homotopy equivalence and which is minimal with that property, meaning that any quotient $Y\to Z$ that is a weak equivalence, must be a homeomorphism. The space $Y$ we obtain is an Alexandroff space: a space in which arbitrary intersections of open sets are open. The weak core $Y$ of $X$ is not unique in general. We study homotopy invariants preserved by filtered colimits of Alexandroff spaces. This can be seen as an analogous to Stong's theory of cores of finite topological spaces.
paper.title: Directed systems of A-spaces and weak cores

paper.abstract:
Every connected homotopy type is the classifying space of a small category, but this general result gives little control over the categories involved. We study finite acyclic categorical models and measure their complexity by the number of objects.
  Our main tool is the sink lemma, which describes the addition of a sink as the attachment of a cone along an explicit map. Using it, we determine the minimum number of objects required to model spheres, bouquets of spheres, Moore spaces of cyclic groups, real projective spaces, and lens spaces. We also exhibit infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic rigid minimal models of the sphere.
  To include spaces admitting no finite model, we introduce a truncated invariant measuring the minimum number of objects required for a finite acyclic category to approximate a space through degree n. Spreading a finite monoid over n+1 objects produces such a category with an n-connected map to the monoid's classifying space. For every nontrivial finite group, this bound is optimal, although its classifying space admits no finite acyclic model.
paper.title: How many points does it take to see the homotopy of a space? Minimal acyclic categorical models

paper.abstract: Persistent homology (PH) summarizes the topological features of data that persist across scales, but it is insensitive to many geometric properties. Persistent Laplacians (PLs) address this limitation: for a pair of simplicial complexes in a filtration, the kernel of the persistent Laplacian recovers the persistent Betti number, while its non-zero spectrum carries additional geometric information. However, PLs are defined for individual pairs of filtration values, so analysing a whole filtration requires evaluating many operators that largely contain the same information, and the result is hard to summarize and interpret. In this paper, we show that this redundancy has a precise structure. For each pair of filtration values, we decompose the space of chains underlying the persistent up-Laplacian into the contributions inherited from the neighboring pairs and a remaining part, which we call the new persistent chain space.
